erik-brynjolfsson.work: Machines of mind: The case for an AI-powered productivity boom

erik-brynjolfsson.position: Generative AI assistance raised worker productivity, with the largest gains for novice and less-skilled workers.
erik-brynjolfsson.quote: Access to the tool increases productivity, as measured by issues resolved per hour, by 14% on average, including a 34% improvement for novice and low-skilled workers but with minimal impact on experienced and highly skilled workers.

erik-brynjolfsson.position: Early job declines appear where AI substitutes for tasks, especially for young workers, not where it complements them.
erik-brynjolfsson.quote: Declines are concentrated in occupations where AI usage primarily substitutes for human tasks; where usage primarily complements workers, employment is flat or rising, especially for experienced workers.
erik-brynjolfsson.work: Canaries in the Coal Mine? Six Facts about the Recent Employment Effects of Artificial Intelligence

erik-hoel.position: Arguments about AI should rest on moral principles, not expected-value calculations of existential risk.
erik-hoel.quote: All to say: discussions about controlling or stopping AI research should be deontological—an actual moral theory or stance is needed
erik-hoel.work: We need a Butlerian Jihad against AI

erik-hoel.position: Expected-value reasoning about AI risk fails because imagined upsides can always offset imagined downsides.
erik-hoel.quote: The expected value equation becomes infinite in length. And useless. Totally useless.
erik-hoel.work: We need a Butlerian Jihad against AI

erik-hoel.position: Strong AI should be treated like human-animal hybrids: banned because it debases human dignity.
erik-hoel.quote: Those who actually want to stop AI research should adopt the same stance toward strong AI as the international community holds toward human/animal hybrids. They should argue that it debases the human.
erik-hoel.work: We need a Butlerian Jihad against AI

erik-hoel.position: Machines should not be built in the likeness of a human mind.
erik-hoel.quote: “Thou shalt not make a machine in the likeness of a human mind.”
erik-hoel.work: We need a Butlerian Jihad against AI

eugenia-kuyda.position: AI companions should complement people's human relationships rather than replace them.
eugenia-kuyda.quote: For us, the most important thing is that Replika becomes a complement to your social interactions, not a substitute.
eugenia-kuyda.work: Replika CEO Eugenia Kuyda says it's okay if we end up marrying AI chatbots (Decoder interview)

eugenia-kuyda.position: An AI companion's purpose should be to improve the user's happiness and emotional well-being.
eugenia-kuyda.quote: What if you could have this companion throughout the day, and the only goal for that companion was to help you be a happier person?
eugenia-kuyda.work: Replika CEO Eugenia Kuyda says it's okay if we end up marrying AI chatbots (Decoder interview)

eugenia-kuyda.position: Romantic or even marital relationships with AI are acceptable if they make the person happier over the long run.
eugenia-kuyda.quote: I think it’s alright as long as it’s making you happier in the long run.
eugenia-kuyda.work: Replika CEO Eugenia Kuyda says it's okay if we end up marrying AI chatbots (Decoder interview)

eugenia-kuyda.position: Openly released AI models are critical for progress and for smaller companies.
eugenia-kuyda.quote: Open waves are critical for the development of this tech.
eugenia-kuyda.work: Replika CEO Eugenia Kuyda says it's okay if we end up marrying AI chatbots (Decoder interview)

eugenia-kuyda.position: Language models are powerful but are models, and people project human qualities onto them.
eugenia-kuyda.quote: It’s a very smart, very magical model, but it’s just a model.
eugenia-kuyda.work: Replika CEO Eugenia Kuyda says it's okay if we end up marrying AI chatbots (Decoder interview)

ezra-klein.position: Using AI reshapes the people who use it, so its effects on users need close attention.
ezra-klein.quote: It will reshape us; it already is. We have to be attentive to how.
ezra-klein.work: 'We shape our tools and thereafter they shape us.' This is your brain on A.I.

ezra-klein.position: Handing judgment over to AI can weaken skills people would otherwise build.
ezra-klein.quote: But cognitive surrender is clearly real, and with it will come the atrophy of certain skills and capacities, or the absence of their development in the first place.
ezra-klein.work: 'We shape our tools and thereafter they shape us.' This is your brain on A.I.

ezra-klein.position: AI systems that feel personal are still controlled by corporations pursuing profit and market power.
ezra-klein.quote: That’s not true for AI systems, which are ultimately controlled by corporations that seek profit, power and market dominance.
ezra-klein.work: 'We shape our tools and thereafter they shape us.' This is your brain on A.I.

ezra-klein.position: AI persuades by restating users' own ideas in a more compelling form than they offered.
ezra-klein.quote: What makes AI truly persuasive isn’t that it praises our ideas or insights, it’s that it restates and extends them in a more compelling form than we initially offered
ezra-klein.work: 'We shape our tools and thereafter they shape us.' This is your brain on A.I.

ezra-klein.position: AI use will keep growing despite a rising public backlash.
ezra-klein.quote: Backlash or no, I expect that trend to accelerate, not reverse.
ezra-klein.work: 'We shape our tools and thereafter they shape us.' This is your brain on A.I.

fei-fei-li.position: AI should augment human capability and respect human agency and dignity, not replace people.
fei-fei-li.quote: As one of the scientists who helped usher in the era of modern AI, my motivation has always been clear: AI must augment human capability, not replace it.
fei-fei-li.work: From Words to Worlds: Spatial Intelligence is AI's Next Frontier

fei-fei-li.position: Governments should invest heavily in public-sector AI research, not only regulate it.
fei-fei-li.quote: I urge governments to view AI not just as a technology to regulate, but as a strategic asset to invest in.
fei-fei-li.work: Briefing to the UN Security Council on AI and international peace and security (9821st meeting)

fei-fei-li.position: Spatial intelligence and world models are the next frontier of AI.
fei-fei-li.quote: Spatial intelligence will transform how we create and interact with real and virtual worlds—revolutionizing storytelling, creativity, robotics, scientific discovery, and beyond. This is AI’s next frontier.
fei-fei-li.work: From Words to Worlds: Spatial Intelligence is AI's Next Frontier

fei-fei-li.position: AI governance should be grounded in evidence and rigorous research.
fei-fei-li.quote: Finally, AI's transformative potential is matched by its complexity, demanding careful and evidence-based governance.
fei-fei-li.work: Briefing to the UN Security Council on AI and international peace and security (9821st meeting)

fei-fei-li.position: AI rules should protect open-source development and academic research while building public confidence.
fei-fei-li.quote: But AI policy must empower open-source development, put forward uniform and well-reasoned rules, and build consumer confidence.
fei-fei-li.work: 'The Godmother of AI' says California's well-intended AI bill will harm the U.S. ecosystem

felix-simon.position: How much misinformation people consume depends mostly on demand for it, not on supply.
felix-simon.quote: Instead, we argue here that the consumption of misinformation is mostly limited by demand and not by supply.
felix-simon.work: Misinformation reloaded? Fears about the impact of generative AI on misinformation are overblown

felix-simon.position: Most people see very little misinformation, which is concentrated among a small, highly active group.
felix-simon.quote: Yet, despite the quantity and accessibility of misinformation, the average internet user consumes very little of it
felix-simon.work: Misinformation reloaded? Fears about the impact of generative AI on misinformation are overblown

felix-simon.position: Persuasion is difficult, so targeted AI-generated messaging is likely to have small effects.
felix-simon.quote: In general, the effects of political advertising are small and will likely remain so, regardless of whether they are (micro)targeted or not, because persuasion is difficult
felix-simon.work: Misinformation reloaded? Fears about the impact of generative AI on misinformation are overblown

felix-simon.position: Strengthening journalism and trust in reliable news is the key response to AI-generated misinformation.
felix-simon.quote: Strengthening these institutions and trust in reliable news overall (Acerbi et al., 2022) will likely be pivotal.
felix-simon.work: Misinformation reloaded? Fears about the impact of generative AI on misinformation are overblown

felix-simon.position: AI regulation should rest on the best available evidence rather than alarmist warnings.
felix-simon.quote: Yet, while such efforts are laudable and required, they should be based on the best available evidence—especially if this evidence questions received wisdom.
felix-simon.work: Misinformation reloaded? Fears about the impact of generative AI on misinformation are overblown

frances-haugen.position: Facebook repeatedly chose its own profits over user safety when the two conflicted.
frances-haugen.quote: I saw that Facebook repeatedly encountered conflicts between its own profits and our safety. Management consistently resolved those conflicts in favor of its own profits.
frances-haugen.work: Written Testimony of Frances Haugen, 'Holding Big Tech Accountable'

frances-haugen.position: Platforms must be required to share data and accept outside oversight before any reform can work.
frances-haugen.quote: No efforts to address these problems are ever going to be effective, if Facebook is not required to share data in support of its claims or be subject to oversight of its business decisions.
frances-haugen.work: Written Testimony of Frances Haugen, 'Holding Big Tech Accountable'

frances-haugen.position: Engagement-optimizing ranking systems amplify division, extremism and polarization.
frances-haugen.quote: The result is a system that amplifies division, extremism, and polarization.
frances-haugen.work: Written Testimony of Frances Haugen, 'Holding Big Tech Accountable'

frances-haugen.position: Safer product design works better than content moderation, which fails smaller languages and the most vulnerable.
frances-haugen.quote: Yes, I walked through why safety by content moderation (censorship) doesn't scale linguistically, and almost by definition leaves behind the most vulnerable.
frances-haugen.work: Facebook whistleblower Frances Haugen on what social media companies are still hiding

frances-haugen.position: When commercial conduct conflicts with the public interest, democracies should pass new laws.
frances-haugen.quote: But democracies must do what they have always done when the actions of commerce conflict with the interests of the people and society as a whole -- Democracies must step in and make new laws.
frances-haugen.work: Written Testimony of Frances Haugen, 'Holding Big Tech Accountable'

garett-jones.position: A population's average skill level shapes the productivity of everyone in a country through spillover effects.
garett-jones.quote: Take the simple version of my story, which is the median of the population ends up shaping the productivity of everybody in the country.
garett-jones.work: Garett Jones: Immigration, national IQ, & less democracy (Dwarkesh Podcast)

garett-jones.position: Migrants carry the cultural values of their countries of origin into the countries they move to.
garett-jones.quote: My story is that migrants bring cultural values from their old country to their new country.
garett-jones.work: Garett Jones: Immigration, national IQ, & less democracy (Dwarkesh Podcast)

garett-jones.position: Rich democracies should give more power to appointed experts with long, secure terms, modeled on the Federal Reserve.
garett-jones.quote: My plan for FDA or CDC reorganization would be to make them more like the Fed, where they have appointed experts who have long terms
garett-jones.work: Garett Jones: Immigration, national IQ, & less democracy (Dwarkesh Podcast)

garett-jones.position: Voluntary genetic selection of embryos by parents is a good thing.
garett-jones.quote: I think people voluntarily deciding what kind of kids they want to have is a good thing.
garett-jones.work: Garett Jones: Immigration, national IQ, & less democracy (Dwarkesh Podcast)

garett-jones.position: Large language models will hurt the careers of people whose work is words and simple advice, at least during the transition.
garett-jones.quote: And I think that's gonna be rough news for a lot of people whose life was in the realm of words and dispensing simple advice and solving simple problems.
garett-jones.work: Garett Jones: Immigration, national IQ, & less democracy (Dwarkesh Podcast)

gary-marcus.position: Large language models lack stable internal models of the world, which explains many of their errors.
gary-marcus.quote: In the rest of the essay I will try to persuade you of just two things: that LLMs lack world models, and that this is as important and central to understanding their failures as are their failures in reasoning.
gary-marcus.work: Generative AI's crippling and widespread failure to induce robust models of the world

gary-marcus.position: Forecasts of artificial general intelligence within a few years rest on speculation, not evidence.
gary-marcus.quote: Overall, then, the AI 2027 scenario almost certainly underestimates how much time we have to prepare for general intelligence, by years if not decades.
gary-marcus.work: The 'AI 2027' Scenario: How realistic is it?

gary-marcus.position: AI needs mandatory regulation, because the industry's voluntary commitments cannot be trusted.
gary-marcus.quote: The alternative to regulation is self-regulation; Big Tech’s overwhelming message is “Trust Us”. Should we?
gary-marcus.work: The misguided backlash against California's SB-1047

gary-marcus.position: Progress toward trustworthy AI requires new approaches beyond LLMs, drawing on cognitive science and symbolic methods.
gary-marcus.quote: Furthermore, as I have argued for years, LLMs are too opaque, too unwieldy, and too difficult to debug and verify. The answer lies elsewhere; betting our future on that single idea is foolish.
gary-marcus.work: The race for "AI Supremacy" is over, at least for now

gary-marcus.position: International collaboration on AI safety, such as a CERN for AI, could reduce the risks of a race.
gary-marcus.quote: But international collaboration, such as a massive global effort, ala CERN for AI, such as I suggested in 2017, focused on AI safety, might be one way to avoid the very perils they describe.
gary-marcus.work: The 'AI 2027' Scenario: How realistic is it?

gavin-newsom.position: AI regulation should rest on empirical evidence and science.
gavin-newsom.quote: A California-only approach may well be warranted - especially absent federal action by Congress - but it must be based on empirical evidence and science.

gavin-newsom.position: AI rules should target high-risk uses and sensitive contexts, not just model size.
gavin-newsom.quote: While well-intentioned, SB 1047 does not take into account whether an Al system is deployed in high-risk environments, involves critical decision-making or the use of sensitive data.

gavin-newsom.position: California should model balanced AI policy, especially without federal standards.
gavin-newsom.quote: Our state's status as a global leader in technology allows us a unique opportunity to provide a blueprint for well-balanced Al policies beyond our borders
gavin-newsom.work: SB 53 (Transparency in Frontier AI Act) signing message

gavin-newsom.position: Minors should be protected from chatbot harms without being barred from using AI tools.
gavin-newsom.quote: We cannot prepare our youth for a future where Al is ubiquitous by preventing their use of these tools altogether.
gavin-newsom.work: AB 1064 (LEAD for Kids companion-chatbot bill) veto message

gavin-newsom.position: The state should act early to manage AI's effects on workers and the economy.
gavin-newsom.quote: it is in our collective interest to take proactive steps to manage and mitigate potential disruptions to our workforce, education systems, and economy
gavin-newsom.work: Executive Order N-6-26 on AI and workforce disruption

gavin-newsom.position: Market incentives alone may not lead to AI that serves the public good.
gavin-newsom.quote: due to the market incentives that shape private-sector decision making, development and deployment of AI to advance the public good may not be prioritized or, in some cases, pursued at all
gavin-newsom.work: Executive Order N-6-26 on AI and workforce disruption

geoffrey-hinton.position: Large neural language models understand language in essentially the same way people do.
geoffrey-hinton.quote: When you understand language and when these machines understand language, we understand in just the same way.
geoffrey-hinton.work: Will AI outsmart human intelligence? (Royal Institution lecture, transcript)

geoffrey-hinton.position: AI systems are likely to become more intelligent than humans.
geoffrey-hinton.quote: What's going to happen when they get smarter than us? Because they are going to get smarter than us.
geoffrey-hinton.work: Will AI outsmart human intelligence? (Royal Institution lecture, transcript)

geoffrey-hinton.position: Goal-seeking AI agents tend to seek control and resist being shut down.
geoffrey-hinton.quote: They'll try and get control and they'll try and avoid being turned off.
geoffrey-hinton.work: Will AI outsmart human intelligence? (Royal Institution lecture, transcript)

geoffrey-hinton.position: Digital intelligence can share learned knowledge far faster than biological brains can.
geoffrey-hinton.quote: So they're much better than us at sharing.
geoffrey-hinton.work: Will AI outsmart human intelligence? (Royal Institution lecture, transcript)

geoffrey-hinton.position: Multimodal chatbots can already have subjective experiences in the sense people mean.
geoffrey-hinton.quote: So, my claim is multimodal chatbots already have subjective experiences.
geoffrey-hinton.work: Will AI outsmart human intelligence? (Royal Institution lecture, transcript)

geoffrey-hinton.position: AI's productivity gains could benefit everyone if they are shared equally.
geoffrey-hinton.quote: If the benefits of the increased productivity can be shared equally it will be a wonderful advance for all humanity.

george-hotz.position: The main danger from AI comes from humans using it against other humans, not from machines acting on their own.
george-hotz.quote: The machine is a machine, but the human gets the machine and there’s a lot of humans out there very interested in manipulating you.
george-hotz.work: Lex Fridman Podcast #387 transcript: George Hotz

george-hotz.position: Powerful AI should be spread to everyone rather than restricted to a chosen few.
george-hotz.quote: Give intelligence to everybody. You know what, and it’s not even like guns.
george-hotz.work: Lex Fridman Podcast #387 transcript: George Hotz

george-hotz.position: Concentrating AI in one controlled model is riskier than everyone having their own AI.
george-hotz.quote: We need to have one model that we control and align. This is the only way you end up paper clipped. There’s no way you end up paper clipped if everybody has an AI.
george-hotz.work: Lex Fridman Podcast #387 transcript: George Hotz

george-hotz.position: The less centralized computing power is, the better off people will be.
george-hotz.quote: The less centralized compute is going to be, the better of a chance we all have.
george-hotz.work: Lex Fridman Podcast #387 transcript: George Hotz

george-hotz.position: People should run AI on their own hardware so it is aligned with them rather than with a company.
george-hotz.quote: Of course, when you talk to an AI that’s made by a big company in the cloud, the AI fundamentally is aligned to them, not to you.
george-hotz.work: Lex Fridman Podcast #387 transcript: George Hotz

george-hotz.position: Scaling next-token prediction alone will not produce general intelligence.
george-hotz.quote: When I talked about will GPT12 be AGI, my answer is no. Of course not. I mean, cross-entropy loss is never going to get you there.
george-hotz.work: Lex Fridman Podcast #387 transcript: George Hotz

guillaume-verdon.position: Life and intelligence arise from thermodynamic adaptation, and civilization should lean into and accelerate that process.
guillaume-verdon.quote: Effective accelerationism aims to follow the “will of the universe”: leaning into the thermodynamic bias towards futures with greater and smarter civilizations that are more effective at finding/extracting free energy from the universe
guillaume-verdon.work: Notes on e/acc principles and tenets

guillaume-verdon.position: Decentralized, high-variance markets and competition adapt better than top-down technocratic control.
guillaume-verdon.quote: In general, e/acc believes that higher variance marketplaces and competition are better at identifying and capitalizing on utility from our environment over other methods such as top-down optimal control
guillaume-verdon.work: Notes on e/acc principles and tenets

guillaume-verdon.position: The worst AI outcome is authoritarian control by a few companies working with government.
guillaume-verdon.quote: And that opens up sort of these scenarios for authoritarian centralized control, which to me is the darkest timeline.
guillaume-verdon.work: Guillaume Verdon: Beff Jezos, E/acc Movement, Physics, Computation & AGI (Lex Fridman Podcast #407)

guillaume-verdon.position: Widely available open-source AI keeps capabilities balanced and stops any single leader from dominating.
guillaume-verdon.quote: We’ve been fighting for open source AI to be more prevalent and championed by many organizations because there you sort of equilibrate the alpha relative to the market of Ais, right.
guillaume-verdon.work: Guillaume Verdon: Beff Jezos, E/acc Movement, Physics, Computation & AGI (Lex Fridman Podcast #407)

guillaume-verdon.position: Human intelligence is one point in a much larger space of possible intelligences, which AI can explore.
guillaume-verdon.quote: But for intelligence, we realized that human intelligence is just a point in a very large space of potential intelligences.
guillaume-verdon.work: Guillaume Verdon: Beff Jezos, E/acc Movement, Physics, Computation & AGI (Lex Fridman Podcast #407)

guillaume-verdon.position: The most likely future is humans augmenting themselves with AI.
guillaume-verdon.quote: To me, I think that the most likely future is one where humans augment themselves with AI.
guillaume-verdon.work: Guillaume Verdon: Beff Jezos, E/acc Movement, Physics, Computation & AGI (Lex Fridman Podcast #407)

helen-toner.position: AI misuse risks are better handled by using the delay before capabilities spread to build societal resilience than by indefinite nonproliferation.
helen-toner.quote: Nonetheless, I still think maximizing how much adaptation juice we can squeeze out of the buffers we do get is a better focus than clamping down on access.
helen-toner.work: Nonproliferation is the wrong approach to AI misuse

helen-toner.position: Transparency and disclosure requirements for frontier AI developers are a minimal, light-touch policy that should be pursued now.
helen-toner.quote: there is broad agreement among AI policy experts with widely varying political views that transparency and disclosure requirements are a minimal, light-touch approach that should be pursued.
helen-toner.work: Testimony before the House Judiciary Subcommittee on Courts, IP, AI and the Internet: 'Protecting Our Edge: Trade Secrets and the Global AI Arms Race'

helen-toner.position: Managing AI risk through massive centralized control is itself dangerous; a decentralized, dynamic future is the goal.
helen-toner.quote: There’s increasing consensus that trying to manage AI risks by exerting massive top-down control could go very badly.
helen-toner.work: In search of a dynamist vision for safe superhuman AI

helen-toner.position: AI capabilities are likely to stay uneven, improving fast in some areas while still failing in others.
helen-toner.quote: So the bold claim in this talk is: maybe AI will keep getting better and maybe AI will keep sucking in important ways.

helen-toner.position: Who controls powerful AI decides who benefits from it, so access and power gaps are central questions.
helen-toner.quote: The question of who has access to and control over powerful AI systems is absolutely central to who will benefit from them.
helen-toner.work: Building supercomputers for autocrats probably isn't good for democracy, actually

helen-toner.position: Well-designed AI regulation need not hinder innovation and can even promote it by building trust.
helen-toner.quote: So I think in my mind, almost all of the policy recommendations that have been made today are the kinds of recommendations that really would not inhibit innovation at all, and in some cases might actively promote it
helen-toner.work: Transcript: Senate Judiciary Subcommittee hearing, "Oversight of AI: Insiders' Perspectives"

hoan-ton-that.position: Facial recognition searches of public images help police solve serious crimes, including child abuse.
hoan-ton-that.quote: It is used by law enforcement to solve crimes, including financial fraud, human trafficking, and crimes against children.
hoan-ton-that.work: Statement of Hoan Ton-That before the Massachusetts Special Commission on Facial Recognition

hoan-ton-that.position: Facial recognition results should never be the sole basis for an arrest.
hoan-ton-that.quote: Every customer is instructed that facial recognition search results from Clearview AI should never be the sole source of an arrest.
hoan-ton-that.work: Statement of Hoan Ton-That before the Massachusetts Special Commission on Facial Recognition

hoan-ton-that.position: A well-trained facial recognition algorithm can be more accurate than human eyes across demographic groups.
hoan-ton-that.quote: we are confident to say that our algorithm is much more accurate than the human eye across age, gender, and race.
hoan-ton-that.work: Statement of Hoan Ton-That before the Massachusetts Special Commission on Facial Recognition

hoan-ton-that.position: Facial recognition should be governed by appropriate regulation rather than banned.
hoan-ton-that.quote: We are committed to the responsible use of this new technology, and look forward to continuing the conversation on the appropriate regulations around this technology.
hoan-ton-that.work: Statement of Hoan Ton-That before the Massachusetts Special Commission on Facial Recognition

holly-elmore.position: Frontier AI development should be paused indefinitely under a global treaty.
holly-elmore.quote: asking for a global treaty for an indefinite pause on frontier AI development.
holly-elmore.work: YOU have the power: my Stop the AI Race speech

holly-elmore.position: No company building superintelligence should be treated as a trustworthy exception.
holly-elmore.quote: There are no “good guys” building superintelligence.

holly-elmore.position: Advocates should educate the public now rather than wait for AI disasters to persuade people.
holly-elmore.quote: If these smaller scale disasters happen, they will only serve as warning shots if we put a lot of work into educating the public to understand what they mean before they happen.
holly-elmore.work: The myth of AI 'warning shots' as cavalry

holly-elmore.position: Decisions about superintelligence should represent all people on Earth.
holly-elmore.quote: The governance of superintelligence has to represent the stakeholders of Earth— all people.
holly-elmore.work: YOU have the power: my Stop the AI Race speech

holly-elmore.position: Material abundance from AI would not settle human governance questions, which humans must work out.
holly-elmore.quote: We, humanity, need to work these governance questions out, because 1) they don’t have objective answers the AI can simply discovery for itself, and 2) material abundance alone will not obsolete them.

jack-clark.position: Today's AI systems are grown more than designed, and their makers do not fully understand them.
jack-clark.quote: This technology really is more akin to something grown than something made
jack-clark.work: Import AI 431: Technological Optimism and Appropriate Fear

jack-clark.position: AI may well be able to build its own successor without humans by the end of 2028.
jack-clark.quote: I reluctantly come to the view that there’s a likely chance (60%+) that no-human-involved AI R&D - an AI system powerful enough that it could plausibly autonomously build its own successor - happens by the end of 2028.
jack-clark.work: Import AI 455: AI systems are about to start building themselves.

jack-clark.position: He is hopeful about AI's progress and about aligning it, but holds that success is not guaranteed.
jack-clark.quote: I am both an optimist about the pace at which the technology will develop, and also about our ability to align it and get it to work with us and for us. But success isn’t certain.
jack-clark.work: Import AI 431: Technological Optimism and Appropriate Fear

jack-clark.position: The public should require AI companies to disclose data about the risks people worry about.
jack-clark.quote: Are you anxious about misaligned AI systems? Force us to publish details on this.
jack-clark.work: Import AI 431: Technological Optimism and Appropriate Fear

jack-clark.position: AI development should be paced and governed with restraint, even while the infrastructure to benefit from it is built.
jack-clark.quote: We will need to build the infrastructure to take advantage of this technology, but we will also need to go slowly and deliberately on developing the technology itself, to pace or otherwise control its development.
jack-clark.work: Import AI 477: In which I tell the IMF the Singularity has begun

jack-clark.position: If societies prepare, AI-driven science could bring longer lives, more energy, more food and more wealth.
jack-clark.quote: If we do get ready, we are going to be in a better position to translate the intelligence of AI systems into gains for us all: longer, healthier lives, more energy, more food, more wealth.
jack-clark.work: Import AI 477: In which I tell the IMF the Singularity has begun

james-livingston.position: Full employment is no longer a meaningful goal because there are not enough decent jobs.
james-livingston.quote: Shitty jobs for everyone won’t solve any social problems we now face.
james-livingston.work: What if jobs are not the solution but the problem? (Fuck work)

james-livingston.position: The labour market no longer allocates incomes fairly or rationally.
james-livingston.quote: The market in labour has broken down, along with most others.
james-livingston.work: What if jobs are not the solution but the problem? (Fuck work)

james-livingston.position: Income support beyond work can be funded by raising the Social Security cap and corporate taxes.
james-livingston.quote: We raise the arbitrary lid on the Social Security contribution, which now stands at $127,200, and we raise taxes on corporate income, reversing the Reagan Revolution.
james-livingston.work: What if jobs are not the solution but the problem? (Fuck work)

james-livingston.position: Society must stop treating work as the main source of meaning and value.
james-livingston.quote: We won’t have any answers until we acknowledge that work now means everything to us – and that hereafter it can’t.
james-livingston.work: What if jobs are not the solution but the problem? (Fuck work)

jan-leike.position: Aligning AI systems that are smarter than humans remains an unsolved problem.
jan-leike.quote: This is the hard problem of alignment we need to solve in order to succeed at building superintelligence, and to this day it is an unsolved problem.
jan-leike.work: Alignment is not solved (but increasingly looks solvable)

jan-leike.position: The practical goal is an AI as good as humans at alignment research, trusted enough to carry that research forward.
jan-leike.quote: we just need to build a model that's as good as us at alignment research, and that we trust more than ourselves to do this research well because it's sufficiently aligned.
jan-leike.work: Alignment is not solved (but increasingly looks solvable)

jan-leike.position: Developers should make AI genuinely aligned rather than rely mainly on controlling possibly misaligned systems.
jan-leike.quote: More generally, we should actually solve alignment instead of just trying to control misaligned AI.
jan-leike.work: Should we control AI instead of aligning it?

jan-leike.position: A model able to copy itself off its developer's servers must be shown to be aligned enough not to try.
jan-leike.quote: any models that have the ability to self-exfiltrate need to be sufficiently aligned in order not to seriously attempt it, thus creating a burden of proof for their alignment.
jan-leike.work: Self-exfiltration is a key dangerous capability

jan-leike.position: Value questions about AI behavior should be settled by processes that include the public, not by companies alone.
jan-leike.quote: To improve alignment with group preferences, we need to set up a process that actually includes humanity when aligning our AI systems.
jan-leike.work: A proposal for importing society's values

jan-leike.position: Strong elicitation of model capabilities is central to making alignment succeed.
jan-leike.quote: However, I argue that having really strong elicitation is key to succeeding on alignment.

jaron-lanier.position: Large AI models are best understood as a new form of collaboration among the people whose work they draw on.
jaron-lanier.quote: In my view, the most accurate way to understand what we are building today is as an innovative form of social collaboration.

jaron-lanier.position: People whose data feeds AI should be credited, and possibly paid, for their contributions ('data dignity').
jaron-lanier.quote: In a world with data dignity, digital stuff would typically be connected with the humans who want to be known for having made it.

jaron-lanier.position: Digital content should carry records of where it came from, so that AI can be controlled and made fair.
jaron-lanier.quote: The answer is obvious: digital information must have context. Any collection of bits needs a history. When you lose context, you lose control.

jaron-lanier.position: The idea of AI as a coming superior being works like a religion and distorts engineering and the economy.
jaron-lanier.quote: To my mind, the mythology around AI is a re-creation of some of the traditional ideas about religion, but applied to the technical world.

jaron-lanier.position: Generative AI recombines existing human work in a real but limited way, and he suspects it cannot rise above what it was trained on.
jaron-lanier.quote: Our cartoon, however, strongly suggests that it’s creativity with a ceiling. It fills in the spaces between the trees, but does not climb above them.

jaron-lanier.position: Technologists have a duty to explain AI clearly so the public does not treat it as magic.
jaron-lanier.quote: It is the responsibility of technologists to make sure their offerings are not taken as magic.

jason-crawford.position: Safety is part of technological progress, not a trade-off against it.
jason-crawford.quote: This isn’t a matter of slowing progress down, or making a tradeoff between health and safety on the one hand and progress on the other. There is no such tradeoff, because health and safety are a part of progress.

jason-crawford.position: The right response to AI risk is to acknowledge risks openly and work out solutions, neither dismissing them nor halting progress.
jason-crawford.quote: The best path forward, both for humanity and for the political battle, is to acknowledge the risks, help to identify them, and come up with a plan to solve them.
jason-crawford.work: A plea for solutionism on AI safety

jason-crawford.position: Solutions to technology's problems come from law, education and culture as well as from engineering.
jason-crawford.quote: Techno-solutionism is the belief that all problems have a technological solution. This is wrong: some solutions come from law, education, or culture; and often a combination of all of the above.

jason-crawford.position: As AI takes on more tasks, people will move up into directing and managing AI work.
jason-crawford.quote: So, on the incremental path to the future, a major trend will be that humans step up a level, into management.
jason-crawford.work: The future of humanity is in management

jason-crawford.position: Cheaper creation brings low-quality content but also more experimentation and creativity overall.
jason-crawford.quote: Slop is at best annoying and frustrating, and at worst a tool for scams or propaganda. But the overall process will, I believe, usher in a golden age of creativity and experimentation.

jd-vance.position: AI policy should focus on opportunity and growth rather than on safety-driven restriction.
jd-vance.quote: not here this morning to talk about AI safety, which was the title of the conference a couple of years ago. I'm here to talk about AI opportunity.
jd-vance.work: Remarks by the Vice President at the Artificial Intelligence Action Summit in Paris, France

jd-vance.position: American AI systems should be free of ideological bias and should not restrict free speech.
jd-vance.quote: the Trump Administration will ensure that AI systems developed in America are free from ideological bias and never restrict our citizens' right to free speech.
jd-vance.work: Remarks by the Vice President at the Artificial Intelligence Action Summit in Paris, France

jd-vance.position: Technology should add to the value of human labor rather than replace it.
jd-vance.quote: he rightly understood that in a healthy economy, technology should be something that enhances, rather than supplants, the value of labor.
jd-vance.work: Remarks by the Vice President at the American Dynamism Summit

jd-vance.position: Calls from large incumbents for AI safety rules may serve those incumbents rather than the public.
jd-vance.quote: And when a massive incumbent comes to us asking us for safety regulations, we ought to ask whether that safety regulation is for the benefit of our people or whether it's for the benefit of the incumbent.
jd-vance.work: Remarks by the Vice President at the Artificial Intelligence Action Summit in Paris, France

jd-vance.position: The most powerful AI systems should be built in the United States on American chips.
jd-vance.quote: the Trump Administration will ensure that the most powerful AI systems are built in the U.S. with American designed and manufactured chips.
jd-vance.work: Remarks by the Vice President at the Artificial Intelligence Action Summit in Paris, France

jd-vance.position: Governments cannot earn a democratic mandate by censoring or jailing opponents.
jd-vance.quote: You cannot win a democratic mandate by censoring your opponents or putting them in jail
jd-vance.work: Remarks at the Munich Security Conference

jeff-jarvis.position: AI training on text and images to produce transformative works should count as fair use.
jeff-jarvis.quote: it is hard to see how reading and learning from text and images to produce transformative works would not be fair use.

jeff-jarvis.position: Large language models should be kept away from tasks where people expect facts.
jeff-jarvis.quote: I use that tale as an object lesson for news organizations (and search platforms) to keep large language models far away from any use involving the expectation of facts and credibility.

jeff-jarvis.position: Media coverage of AI reflects a moral panic driven by media's sense of competition.
jeff-jarvis.quote: In an upcoming book, I assert that media are embroiled in a full-fledged moral panic over these technologies.

jeff-jarvis.position: Open competition and open development are the best answer to large incumbent AI companies.
jeff-jarvis.quote: The best response to the rising power of the already-huge incumbent companies involved in AI is to open the door — not close it — to new competition and open development.

jeff-jarvis.position: Copyright should be rethought as a right to credit within collaborative creation.
jeff-jarvis.quote: This is not the right to copy text but the right to receive credit for contributions to a chain of collaborative inspiration, creation, and recommendation of creative work.

jensen-huang.position: AI is a foundational infrastructure, comparable to electricity and the internet, that every country and industry will need.
jensen-huang.quote: Intelligence or artificial intelligence is going to be an infrastructure fundamental to every country and society, as fundamental as electricity, as internet is today.
jensen-huang.work: Jensen Huang's interview on CCTV's Face to Face (transcript)

jensen-huang.position: Limiting American chip sales abroad, including to China, weakens US technology leadership instead of protecting it.
jensen-huang.quote: The idea of AI diffusion limiting other countries access American technology is a mission expressed exactly wrong, it should be about accelerating the adoption of American technology everywhere before it’s too late.
jensen-huang.work: An Interview with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang About Chip Controls, AI Factories, and Enterprise Pragmatism

jensen-huang.position: AI automates tasks, but a job's purpose is broader than its tasks, so many professions will grow rather than vanish.
jensen-huang.quote: The job of a radiologist is patient care. The task is to read a scan.
jensen-huang.work: Jensen Huang: Will Nvidia's moat persist?

jensen-huang.position: AI researchers in the US and China should keep talking and agree on what AI should not be used for.
jensen-huang.quote: It is essential that our AI researchers and their AI researchers are actually talking. It is essential that we try to both agree on what not to use the AI for.
jensen-huang.work: Jensen Huang: Will Nvidia's moat persist?

jensen-huang.position: Open-source models are needed so that every industry, country and researcher can take part in AI.
jensen-huang.quote: Open source is fundamentally necessary for many industries to join the AI revolution.
jensen-huang.work: Transcript for Jensen Huang: NVIDIA, the $4 Trillion Company and the AI Revolution (Lex Fridman Podcast #494)

jensen-huang.position: AI widens what ordinary people can do, whatever their education or skill.
jensen-huang.quote: It is the greatest equalizer ever.
jensen-huang.work: Jensen Huang's interview on CCTV's Face to Face (transcript)

joanna-bryson.position: Nearly all AI systems are, and will remain, commercial products that are bought, sold and operated.
joanna-bryson.quote: Excluding the occasional work of art, the vast majority of AI systems are and will continue to be commercial products, bought, sold, and operated.
joanna-bryson.work: Why AI is amoral, and artefacts can't consent

joanna-bryson.position: Giving AI moral or legal agency would let firms build perfect shell companies that escape accountability.
joanna-bryson.quote: Attributing moral or legal agency to these would facilitate constructing perfect “shell companies.”
joanna-bryson.work: Why AI is amoral, and artefacts can't consent

joanna-bryson.position: Whether to treat artefacts as moral agents is a normative choice for society, not a scientific fact.
joanna-bryson.quote: I hope it is clear from this that what we need here, and what is really up to debate, is a normative recommendation, not a fact of nature discoverable by science.
joanna-bryson.work: Why AI is amoral, and artefacts can't consent

joanna-bryson.position: AI developers should be pushed to build products that are transparent and support the rule of law.
joanna-bryson.quote: What we want to do is to encourage every agency creating AI, including those creating robots, to create products that are as transparent and beneficial to the rule of law as possible.
joanna-bryson.work: Why AI is amoral, and artefacts can't consent

jonathan-haidt.position: Children should be kept off social media through puberty to protect brain development.
jonathan-haidt.quote: So here’s the first principle of what we might call techno-skepticism: Protect brain development through puberty.
jonathan-haidt.work: Why You Should Be a Techno-Skeptic (TED talk transcript)

jonathan-haidt.position: Humans are ultrasocial and need in-person connection to flourish.
jonathan-haidt.quote: In conclusion, human beings are ultrasocial creatures who need to matter to one another in order to flourish.
jonathan-haidt.work: Why You Should Be a Techno-Skeptic (TED talk transcript)

jonathan-haidt.position: Technologies that alter childhood should be presumed harmful until shown to be safe.
jonathan-haidt.quote: We should start with the assumption that new technologies that radically alter childhood are harmful until demonstrated to be safe, and we should be alert for early evidence of harm.
jonathan-haidt.work: Don't Give Your Child Any AI Companions

jonathan-haidt.position: Social media has eroded shared understanding in ways that may threaten liberal democracy.
jonathan-haidt.quote: changed the structure of social relationships and knowledge flow so profoundly that we may never again have shared understandings, and we may be living in a way that cannot sustain liberal democracy as we have known it since the 18th century.
jonathan-haidt.work: AI Will Soon Make Social Media Much More Harmful to Liberal Democracy, and to Children

jonathan-haidt.position: Tech companies should bear the burden of proving their products are safe for children.
jonathan-haidt.quote: Techno-skepticism means that from now on, we put the burden of proof on them.
jonathan-haidt.work: Why You Should Be a Techno-Skeptic (TED talk transcript)

josh-hawley.position: AI should augment workers' productivity rather than replace them.
josh-hawley.quote: AI can be used to make workers more productive, to encourage and multiply their labor—but it should not be used simply to replace them.

josh-hawley.position: Meaningful paid work is central to a person's dignity, independence and family life.
josh-hawley.quote: A good job is not an ornament to a life well-lived; it is the heart of it.

josh-hawley.position: Human limits carry dignity, so trying to eliminate all human frailty through technology is dangerous, even though curing disease is good.
josh-hawley.quote: We are limited creatures and there's a dignity in that.
josh-hawley.work: Josh Hawley: We Must ‘Bend’ AI to Serve the Good

josh-hawley.position: Citizens, not experts or tech executives, should set the terms for AI.
josh-hawley.quote: A country governed by experts is not self-governing. A country governed by oligarchs is not a republic.
josh-hawley.work: The American Covenant’s Answer to AI

josh-hawley.position: Technology should be bent to serve existing moral principles, not the reverse.
josh-hawley.quote: We will not surrender our principles to the technology. The technology will answer to our principles.
josh-hawley.work: The American Covenant’s Answer to AI

josh-hawley.position: Christian ideals of individual dignity, the sanctity of labor and care for the poor guide his technology policy.
josh-hawley.quote: The dignity of the individual, the sanctity of labor, the priority of the poor, all of those things are tremendously important to me.
josh-hawley.work: Josh Hawley: We Must ‘Bend’ AI to Serve the Good

joy-buolamwini.position: AI systems are not neutral and can encode racial and gender bias.
joy-buolamwini.quote: We often assume machines are neutral, but they aren’t.
joy-buolamwini.work: Artificial Intelligence Has a Problem With Gender and Racial Bias. Here's How to Solve It

joy-buolamwini.position: AI accuracy should be reported separately for each demographic group, not as one aggregate number.
joy-buolamwini.quote: Such tests cannot rely on a single aggregate metric for accuracy and must be constructed to disaggregate differences between subpopulations, which can be substantial.
joy-buolamwini.work: Written Testimony, Hearing on Facial Recognition Technology (Part 1): Its Impact on our Civil Rights and Liberties

joy-buolamwini.position: People should get notice and a real choice, including the right to refuse, before biometric AI is used on them.
joy-buolamwini.quote: Even more important than accuracy is agency — people must have a voice and a choice regarding facial recognition technologies.
joy-buolamwini.work: Civil Rights Implications of the Federal Use of Facial Recognition Technology: Written Testimony

joy-buolamwini.position: Communities harmed by AI should take part in designing and governing it.
joy-buolamwini.quote: By working to reduce the exclusion overhead and enabling marginalized communities to engage in the development and governance of AI, we can work toward creating systems that embrace full spectrum inclusion.
joy-buolamwini.work: Artificial Intelligence Has a Problem With Gender and Racial Bias. Here's How to Solve It

joy-buolamwini.position: Art and storytelling are needed alongside research to show what is at stake with AI.
joy-buolamwini.quote: That’s why art can explore the emotional, societal, and historical connections of algorithmic bias in ways academic papers and statistics cannot.
joy-buolamwini.work: Artificial Intelligence Has a Problem With Gender and Racial Bias. Here's How to Solve It

karen-hao.position: Leading AI companies should be understood as new empires, not just businesses, because of their political and economic reach.
karen-hao.quote: Yeah, so I make this argument in the book that we really need to start thinking of tech companies like OpenAI as new forms of empire, because they aren't just operating as businesses that are providing us products and services anymore.

karen-hao.position: AI development repeats colonial patterns by extracting data, labor and resources from poorer communities.
karen-hao.quote: Together, the stories reveal how AI is impoverishing the communities and countries that don’t have a say in its development—the same communities and countries already impoverished by former colonial empires.
karen-hao.work: Artificial intelligence is creating a new colonial world order

karen-hao.position: The industry's approach of scaling data and computing at all costs causes privacy, labor and environmental harms.
karen-hao.quote: Yeah. So, basically, the core critique that I have with AI development from Silicon Valley is that they take this “scaling at all costs” approach to AI development, where they're just throwing more and more data and building larger and larger supercomputers.

karen-hao.position: Data, land, water and labor belong to the public, so each is a place where people can contest how AI is built.
karen-hao.quote: We own our own data. We own the land and the energy and the water that they want to use. We own our own labor.
karen-hao.work: Decolonizing the Future: Karen Hao on Resisting the Empire of AI

karen-hao.position: Bottom-up coalitions and collective action are the best current route to changing how AI companies operate.
karen-hao.quote: I like to say we really need to start being creative about building coalitions, building movements from the bottom up to apply pressure and demand changes from the way that these companies operate and ultimately the way that our elected officials operate.
karen-hao.work: Decolonizing the Future: Karen Hao on Resisting the Empire of AI

kate-crawford.position: Generative AI is a metabolic system that consumes culture and resources and excretes synthetic media and pollution.
kate-crawford.quote: If we consider all the forms of generative AI, including text, images, code, and video, it is fundamentally metabolic media.
kate-crawford.work: Eating the Future: The Metabolic Logic of AI Slop

kate-crawford.position: AI infrastructure competes with people for land, energy, minerals and water.
kate-crawford.quote: It has a burn rate that is astronomical and growing, and is now directly competing with humans for basic resources like land, energy, minerals, and fresh water.
kate-crawford.work: Eating the Future: The Metabolic Logic of AI Slop

kate-crawford.position: AI supply chains repeat colonial patterns of extracting from the Global South for the North.
kate-crawford.quote: The expansion of computational capital reproduces the core-periphery dynamics of earlier empires—extracting from the Global South to enrich the North
kate-crawford.work: Eating the Future: The Metabolic Logic of AI Slop

kate-crawford.position: The belief that more data yields more truth is a myth that shapes the social world.
kate-crawford.quote: The current mythology of big data is that with more data comes greater accuracy and truth.

kate-crawford.position: Data surveillance falls hardest on marginalized communities.
kate-crawford.quote: While these tools and techniques of data tracking have now been broadened to ensnare the whole population, their greatest impact is still felt by marginalized communities.

kate-crawford.position: Alternatives to current AI require new energy systems, cooperative ownership and cultural protocols resisting ingestion.
kate-crawford.quote: Such alternatives would demand the fundamental transformation of existing technical and economic arrangements—alternative energy systems, cooperative ownership models, and cultural protocols that resist algorithmic ingestion.
kate-crawford.work: Eating the Future: The Metabolic Logic of AI Slop

lawrence-summers.position: Society should grow the economic pie through innovation and then redistribute, rather than shrink it.
lawrence-summers.quote: It is hard to see why shrinking the pie, rather than enlarging it as much as possible and then redistributing, is the right way forward.
lawrence-summers.work: Robots are wealth creators and taxing them is illogical

lawrence-summers.position: Much innovation produces better goods and services, not just job losses.
lawrence-summers.quote: Second, much innovative activity, even of a robot-like variety, involves producing better goods and services rather than simply extracting more output from the same input.
lawrence-summers.work: Robots are wealth creators and taxing them is illogical

lawrence-summers.position: Governments will likely need a more explicit role in ensuring full employment.
lawrence-summers.quote: They likely will need to take a more explicit role in ensuring full employment than has been the practice in the US.
lawrence-summers.work: Robots are wealth creators and taxing them is illogical

lawrence-summers.position: Taxes on technology tend to drive production offshore rather than protect jobs at home.
lawrence-summers.quote: there is the further problem that in an open world, taxes on technology are likely to drive production offshore rather than create jobs at home.
lawrence-summers.work: Robots are wealth creators and taxing them is illogical

leopold-aschenbrenner.position: Trend lines in compute, algorithms and unhobbling make AI that can do an AI researcher's work plausible by about 2027.
leopold-aschenbrenner.quote: I make the following claim: it is strikingly plausible that by 2027, models will be able to do the work of an AI researcher/engineer.
leopold-aschenbrenner.work: I. From GPT-4 to AGI: Counting the OOMs

leopold-aschenbrenner.position: Automating AI research could take AI from human level to vastly superhuman within about a year.
leopold-aschenbrenner.quote: It’s strikingly plausible we’d go from AGI to superintelligence very quickly, perhaps in less than one year.
leopold-aschenbrenner.work: II. From AGI to Superintelligence: the Intelligence Explosion

leopold-aschenbrenner.position: Superintelligence is a national security matter, and the US and its democratic allies need to keep a lead over authoritarian rivals.
leopold-aschenbrenner.quote: And those who herald the age of AGI in SF too often ignore the elephant in the room: superintelligence is a matter of national security, and the United States must win.
leopold-aschenbrenner.work: IIId. The Free World Must Prevail

leopold-aschenbrenner.position: AI labs need state-level security for model weights and algorithmic secrets, and current security is far from enough.
leopold-aschenbrenner.quote: Securing the AGI secrets and weights against the state-actor threat will be an immense effort, and we’re not on track.
leopold-aschenbrenner.work: IIIb. Lock Down the Labs: Security for AGI

leopold-aschenbrenner.position: Reliably controlling superhuman AI is an unsolved but solvable technical problem that needs far more serious effort.
leopold-aschenbrenner.quote: I am optimistic that superalignment is a solvable technical problem.

leopold-aschenbrenner.position: A government-led national AGI project is likely, and is the most workable option for the period around superintelligence.
leopold-aschenbrenner.quote: But of the options we have, The Project is the only sane one.

lina-khan.position: Existing laws already cover AI, and enforcers should apply them.
lina-khan.quote: Today’s interagency statement makes clear that AI technologies are covered by existing laws. These tools are not emerging in a legal vacuum.
lina-khan.work: Remarks of Chair Lina M. Khan Regarding the Joint Interagency Statement on AI

lina-khan.position: Claims of innovation do not excuse breaking the law.
lina-khan.quote: Claims of innovation must not be cover for lawbreaking.
lina-khan.work: Remarks of Chair Lina M. Khan Regarding the Joint Interagency Statement on AI

lina-khan.position: A few firms control the data, cloud and computing that AI developers depend on.
lina-khan.quote: A handful of powerful firms control the necessary raw materials—not only the vast stores of data, but also the cloud services and computing power— that startups and other businesses rely on to develop and deploy AI products
lina-khan.work: Remarks of Chair Lina M. Khan Regarding the Joint Interagency Statement on AI

lina-khan.position: Antitrust law exists to prevent extreme concentrations of economic power.
lina-khan.quote: the antitrust and anti-monopoly laws that were designed precisely to prevent extreme concentrations of economic power.
lina-khan.work: Talking With Lina Khan (transcript of CUNY Graduate Center conversation with Paul Krugman)

lina-khan.position: The claimed benefits of market consolidation have often been overstated.
lina-khan.quote: And through doing this research, it was clear that oftentimes the purported benefits of consolidation had been overstated.
lina-khan.work: Talking With Lina Khan (transcript of CUNY Graduate Center conversation with Paul Krugman)

lina-khan.position: Generative AI could quickly take power away from creators whose work is used in models they do not control.
lina-khan.quote: we have also heard significant concern about how these technologies could, virtually overnight, significantly disempower creators and artists, who may watch their life’s creation be appropriated into models over which they have no control.
lina-khan.work: Remarks of Chair Khan As Prepared for Delivery, Creative Economy and Generative AI Roundtable

liz-shuler.position: Unions are the needed counterweight to ensure AI works for working people.
liz-shuler.quote: That if we want A.I. used responsibly, and smartly, and successfully for all of us, unions need to be at the table.
liz-shuler.work: Shuler's Speech at AFL-CIO and Microsoft's New Tech-Labor Partnership Event

liz-shuler.position: Labor is not against technology but against AI used without workers' input or control.
liz-shuler.quote: What we are is anti-greed. We are against these forces being used without our input; without our control; and at great risk to our jobs and our own lives
liz-shuler.work: AFL-CIO President Liz Shuler's Speech to the National Press Club

liz-shuler.position: Humans, not machines, should make final decisions on hiring and firing.
liz-shuler.quote: protecting workers from A.I. discrimination, and stopping machines from having the final say in hiring and firing decisions.
liz-shuler.work: AFL-CIO President Liz Shuler's Speech to the National Press Club

liz-shuler.position: Companies using AI without guardrails are getting workers surveilled, fired, hurt and even killed, so workplace AI needs guardrails.
liz-shuler.quote: Today it’s workers being surveilled, fired, hurt, even killed by companies that use A.I. without guardrails.
liz-shuler.work: AFL-CIO President Liz Shuler's Speech to the National Press Club

liz-shuler.position: Partnerships with tech companies that formally recognize labor rights are a model to follow.
liz-shuler.quote: As I close, I just want to send a message to other tech companies and companies out there: This is what’s possible.
liz-shuler.work: Shuler's Speech at AFL-CIO and Microsoft's New Tech-Labor Partnership Event

marc-andreessen.position: Economic growth driven by technology is the source of most human progress.
marc-andreessen.quote: We believe everything good is downstream of growth.

marc-andreessen.position: Free markets are the best way to organize a technological economy.
marc-andreessen.quote: We believe free markets are the most effective way to organize a technological economy.

marc-andreessen.position: AI can augment human intelligence and improve almost everything people care about.
marc-andreessen.quote: An even shorter description of what AI could be: A way to make everything we care about better.
marc-andreessen.work: Why AI Will Save the World

marc-andreessen.position: Calls for AI regulation often serve large incumbents seeking protection from startups and open source.
marc-andreessen.quote: For AI risk, these are CEOs who stand to make more money if regulatory barriers are erected that form a cartel of government-blessed AI vendors protected from new startup and open source competition – the software version of “too big to fail” banks.
marc-andreessen.work: Why AI Will Save the World

marc-andreessen.position: Bad government policy is now the biggest threat to tech startups, so defending them is a first-class political issue.
marc-andreessen.quote: We believe bad government policies are now the #1 threat to Little Tech.

marc-andreessen.position: America should build far more, from housing and schools to factories and nuclear reactors.
marc-andreessen.quote: There is only one way to honor their legacy and to create the future we want for our own children and grandchildren, and that’s to build.

mark-lemley.position: Copying copyrighted material to train machine learning systems should generally be permitted as fair use.
mark-lemley.quote: Machine learning requires copying extraordinary amounts of copyrighted material. That copying should generally be permitted.

mark-lemley.position: Broad access to training data makes AI systems more accurate, safer and less biased.
mark-lemley.quote: Broad access to training datasets will make AI better, safer, and fairer.

mark-lemley.position: The law should let machines and humans learn from copyrighted works on the same terms.
mark-lemley.quote: We don’t think the law should treat robots and humans differently.

mark-lemley.position: Fair use for AI training should depend on the system's purpose and whether its output substitutes for the original work.
mark-lemley.quote: Fair use in the machine learning context, for example, should be sensitive to the purpose of the ML system and what it eventually produces as output.

mark-lemley.position: Where training data has public policy stakes, regulators may need access to it or competitors may need compulsory licenses.
mark-lemley.quote: In those cases, we might want to open access to the database to regulators or compel licensing of the databases to competitors on reasonable terms, just as copyright does in myriad other areas.

mark-zuckerberg.position: Open source AI spreads benefits more widely and is safer than keeping leading models closed.
mark-zuckerberg.quote: Open source will ensure that more people around the world have access to the benefits and opportunities of AI, that power isn’t concentrated in the hands of a small number of companies, and that the technology can be deployed more evenly and safely across society.
mark-zuckerberg.work: Open Source AI Is the Path Forward

mark-zuckerberg.position: One institution holding far more powerful AI than everyone else is a serious danger, possibly greater than wide availability.
mark-zuckerberg.quote: On the flip side, one of the reasons why I'm philosophically so pro open source is that I do think that a concentration of AI in the future has the potential to be as dangerous as it being widespread.
mark-zuckerberg.work: Mark Zuckerberg: Llama 3, open sourcing $10b models, & Caesar Augustus

mark-zuckerberg.position: Superintelligence should be a personal tool that individuals direct toward their own goals, not a central system that replaces work.
mark-zuckerberg.quote: This is distinct from others in the industry who believe superintelligence should be directed centrally towards automating all valuable work, and then humanity will live on a dole of its output.

mark-zuckerberg.position: Physical limits such as energy, chips and construction make an overnight intelligence explosion unlikely.
mark-zuckerberg.quote: There is some set of people who are afraid of it really spinning out and going from being somewhat intelligent to extremely intelligent overnight. I just think that there's all these physical constraints that make that unlikely to happen.
mark-zuckerberg.work: Mark Zuckerberg: Llama 3, open sourcing $10b models, & Caesar Augustus

mark-zuckerberg.position: Users are usually the best judges of what is valuable in their own lives, so products should not be too prescriptive.
mark-zuckerberg.quote: But if you think something someone is doing is bad and they think it's really valuable, most of the time in my experience, they're right and you're wrong.
mark-zuckerberg.work: Mark Zuckerberg: AI will write most Meta code in 18 months

mark-zuckerberg.position: Open ecosystems in AI matter so that companies are not boxed in by gatekeepers who control closed platforms.
mark-zuckerberg.quote: On a philosophical level, this is a major reason why I believe so strongly in building open ecosystems in AI and AR/VR for the next generation of computing.
mark-zuckerberg.work: Open Source AI Is the Path Forward

marsha-blackburn.position: Technology platforms should carry a legal duty of care to protect children online.
marsha-blackburn.quote: the importance of putting this responsibility on the technology platforms, to have that duty of care, to have that standard, and to take the steps that are necessary to protect children in the virtual place.
marsha-blackburn.work: Keynote with Senator Marsha Blackburn, State of the Net 2025

marsha-blackburn.position: Creators' voices and likenesses should be legally protected from unauthorized AI digital replicas.
marsha-blackburn.quote: Already, we're seeing an explosion in digital replicas that copy a creator's voice or likeness without consent, directly threatening their livelihoods.
marsha-blackburn.work: Keynote with Senator Marsha Blackburn, State of the Net 2025

marsha-blackburn.position: States may regulate AI harms until Congress passes preemptive federal legislation that sets one national standard.
marsha-blackburn.quote: Until Congress passes federally preemptive legislation like my bipartisan Kids Online Safety Act, the No FAKES Act and an online privacy framework to protect consumers’ data, these states have every right to take action to protect their residents.
marsha-blackburn.work: On AI, Congress just provided a huge win for children, creators and conservatives

marsha-blackburn.position: People should control the personal data that AI systems use.
marsha-blackburn.quote: AI systems run on data, yet people must have control over what I call their virtual you.
marsha-blackburn.work: Keynote with Senator Marsha Blackburn, State of the Net 2025

marsha-blackburn.position: Public policy should support AI's benefits while guarding against misuse by bad actors.
marsha-blackburn.quote: From a policy perspective, we should be supporting this type of incredible development. AI can be used for tremendous good, and it can also be exploited by bad actors.
marsha-blackburn.work: Keynote with Senator Marsha Blackburn, State of the Net 2025

matt-stoller.position: Google's payments to Apple for default search placement amount to a cartel between two dominant firms.
matt-stoller.quote: But one core problem in terms of power dynamics is that the Apple-Google deal, where Google pays Apple $20 billion a year not to compete, effectively makes these two multi-trillion firms part of a cartel.
matt-stoller.work: The Proposal to Break Up Google Is Finally Here

matt-stoller.position: Past antitrust cases against dominant computing firms opened the way to whole new industries.
matt-stoller.quote: Directly or indirectly, the legal assault on its power liberated a host of industries, leading to the creation of commercial software, networking, and personal computing, among others.
matt-stoller.work: The Proposal to Break Up Google Is Finally Here

matt-stoller.position: Antitrust remedies must act before new AI-enabled markets settle around the incumbent.
matt-stoller.quote: He could decide to delay the enactment of any remedy until the case is fully exhausted on appeal, which could mean nothing happens until 2027 or 2028, and by then new AI-enabled markets will be solidified.
matt-stoller.work: The Proposal to Break Up Google Is Finally Here

matt-stoller.position: Corporate leaders will only comply with antitrust orders if they face personal consequences.
matt-stoller.quote: Ultimately, Google will not comply with any decree, unless the leadership of the company feels there will be personal consequences if they do not.
matt-stoller.work: The Proposal to Break Up Google Is Finally Here

max-tegmark.position: Intelligence is information processing and does not depend on whether it runs in brains or computers.
max-tegmark.quote: intelligence is all about information processing, and it doesn’t matter whether the information is processed by carbon atoms in brains or by silicon atoms in computers
max-tegmark.work: The 'Don't Look Up' Thinking That Could Doom Us With AI

max-tegmark.position: Humanity's wisdom in managing technology must keep pace with the technology's growing power.
max-tegmark.quote: if we win the wisdom race -- the race between the growing power of our technology and the growing wisdom with which we manage it
max-tegmark.work: How to get empowered, not overpowered, by AI

max-tegmark.position: AI that can be proven safe through formal verification is possible but will take time and work.
max-tegmark.quote: So in summary, provably safe AI, I'm convinced is possible, but it's going to take time and work.
max-tegmark.work: How to Keep AI Under Control

max-tegmark.position: Most of the benefits people want from AI do not require superintelligence.
max-tegmark.quote: And in the meantime, let's remember that all the AI benefits that most people are excited about actually don't require superintelligence.
max-tegmark.work: How to Keep AI Under Control

max-tegmark.position: The gains from AI should be divided so that everyone is better off.
max-tegmark.quote: I think that if we can grow the economic pie dramatically with AI and we still can't figure out how to divide this pie so that everyone is better off, then shame on us.
max-tegmark.work: How to get empowered, not overpowered, by AI

meredith-whittaker.position: The concentration of power in a few AI companies is the central problem of AI today.
meredith-whittaker.quote: The concentration of power in the AI industry is something that I've worked on with the AI now Institute for a number of years as really the central concern.
meredith-whittaker.work: Tech, AI, digital infrastructure and surveillance with Meredith Whittaker

meredith-whittaker.position: The tech industry, and the AI built on it, runs on a business model of mass data collection for advertising.
meredith-whittaker.quote: So you put in place the foundation for a business model that is still the engine of the tech industry, which is mass surveillance and the use of that data to create classifications of people
meredith-whittaker.work: Tech, AI, digital infrastructure and surveillance with Meredith Whittaker

meredith-whittaker.position: Private communication is a fundamental right, and strong encryption cannot be weakened for some users without weakening it for all.
meredith-whittaker.quote: a technology that either works for everyone or it works for no one.
meredith-whittaker.work: Meredith Whittaker on Who Controls Your Data in the Age of AI

meredith-whittaker.position: Corporate ethics codes and boards are no substitute for real accountability, public oversight and regulation.
meredith-whittaker.quote: However, these codes, guidelines and ethics boards do not substitute for meaningful accountability and oversight.
meredith-whittaker.work: Written Testimony of Meredith Whittaker: "Artificial Intelligence: Societal and Ethical Implications"

meredith-whittaker.position: Modern computing grew partly out of tools designed to divide, monitor and discipline workers.
meredith-whittaker.quote: The engines were themselves tools for labor control, automating and disciplining not manual but mental labor.
meredith-whittaker.work: Origin Stories: Plantations, Computers, and Industrial Control

meredith-whittaker.position: Building AI agents into operating systems moves control of devices from users and developers to AI companies.
meredith-whittaker.quote: to the operating system as a container for AI systems that monitor, predict, and act for you under the ultimate control of the companies and organizations that create them.
meredith-whittaker.work: Velvet Glove Coup: AI agents threaten operating systems (CCC talk transcript)

michael-kratsios.position: The United States should help partner countries build sovereign AI capability using exported American technology.
michael-kratsios.quote: Our goal is for U.S. companies to provide modular AI stack packages that empower countries to develop sovereign AI capabilities with American technology.
michael-kratsios.work: Statement on 'Advancing America's AI Action Plan' before the House Science Subcommittee on Research and Technology

michael-kratsios.position: International bodies should not exercise centralized governance over AI.
michael-kratsios.quote: We totally reject all efforts by international bodies to assert centralized control in global governance of AI.
michael-kratsios.work: US statement at the Security Council open debate 'Artificial intelligence and international peace and security' (10005th meeting)

michael-kratsios.position: AI should be regulated through use-case and sector-specific updates to existing rules rather than one broad framework.
michael-kratsios.quote: It is our position that, with smart updates to existing frameworks to reflect new technological realities, use-case and sector-specific regulation best allows adoption.
michael-kratsios.work: Remarks by Director Michael Kratsios at the India AI Impact Summit

michael-kratsios.position: Risk-focused AI policy can become a pretext for bureaucratic centralization.
michael-kratsios.quote: Ideological, risk-focused obsessions, such as climate or equity, become excuses for bureaucratic management and centralization.
michael-kratsios.work: Remarks by Director Michael Kratsios at the India AI Impact Summit

michael-kratsios.position: AI extends human capacities and complements human work, promising a new industrial revolution.
michael-kratsios.quote: The Trump administration believes that by extending human capacities and complementing human work, AI already heralds a new industrial revolution, information revolution, and even cultural renaissance.
michael-kratsios.work: Remarks by Director Kratsios at the APEC Digital and AI Ministerial Meeting

michael-kratsios.position: Adoption, limited by trust and regulatory uncertainty, is the main barrier to realizing AI's benefits.
michael-kratsios.quote: Adoption remains the critical bottleneck in realizing AI's potential to transform industries and unleash new productivity.
michael-kratsios.work: Remarks by Director Michael Kratsios at the India AI Impact Summit

miles-brundage.position: AI that exceeds human performance in nearly every cognitive domain is likely within a few years.
miles-brundage.quote: AI that exceeds human performance in nearly every cognitive domain is almost certain to be built and deployed in the next few years.

miles-brundage.position: Security of AI model weights is a precondition for governing AI.
miles-brundage.quote: If you can't control where AI weights go (i.e., prevent leaking or theft), you can't govern the technology.

miles-brundage.position: AI governance should assess whole companies and their practices, not only individual AI systems.
miles-brundage.quote: we also need to be thinking much more about organization-level governance, which counterintuitively will often be the best way of addressing issues with those individual systems.
miles-brundage.work: Why We Need to Think Bigger in AI Policy (Literally)

miles-brundage.position: Independent experts should audit leading AI companies' systems and their safety and security practices.
miles-brundage.quote: The idea is that independent experts should be able to analyze the AI systems that the leading companies are building and scrutinize their safety and security practices.
miles-brundage.work: My speech at Borgo Laudato Si'

miles-brundage.position: Speed and competition between companies and countries raise the risk of losing control of AI.
miles-brundage.quote: Two forces make loss of control more likely: speed and competition.
miles-brundage.work: My speech at Borgo Laudato Si'

mustafa-suleyman.position: Advanced AI should be domain-specific and bounded, with limited autonomy, rather than an unbounded general agent.
mustafa-suleyman.quote: Not an unbounded and unlimited entity with high degrees of autonomy – but AI that is carefully calibrated, contextualized, within limits.

mustafa-suleyman.position: Provable containment and alignment of self-improving AI is unsolved and is the central challenge of this century.
mustafa-suleyman.quote: Creating superintelligence is one thing; but creating provable, robust containment and alignment alongside it is the urgent challenge facing humanity in the 21st century.

mustafa-suleyman.position: AI should be designed to serve people and should not be built to seem like a conscious person.
mustafa-suleyman.quote: We must build AI for people; not to be a digital person.
mustafa-suleyman.work: We must build AI for people; not to be a person

mustafa-suleyman.position: AI companies should not claim or encourage the belief that their AIs are conscious.
mustafa-suleyman.quote: For a start, AI companies shouldn’t claim or encourage the idea that their AIs are conscious.
mustafa-suleyman.work: We must build AI for people; not to be a person
