mustafa-suleyman.position: Autonomy and unsupervised self-improvement are key thresholds where AI risk rises.
mustafa-suleyman.quote: Autonomy is very obviously a threshold over which we increase risk in our society.

mustafa-suleyman.position: Technology has been the main driver of human progress, and its development should be accelerated.
mustafa-suleyman.quote: We should celebrate and accelerate technology because it’s been the greatest engine of human progress in history.

neil-chilson.position: AI is a general-purpose computing paradigm, not a distinct product to regulate.
neil-chilson.quote: But AI isn’t a product, it is a computing paradigm.

neil-chilson.position: Today's state AI bills regulate too early and risk stifling AI the way Red Flag Laws stifled cars.
neil-chilson.quote: The state AI regulations being pushed today risk becoming the Red Flag Laws of the 21st century.

neil-chilson.position: Narrow laws are justified where AI harms are well understood, such as non-consensual pornographic deepfakes.
neil-chilson.quote: I have been supportive, for example, of laws to prohibit the distribution of non-consensual pornographic deepfakes.

neil-chilson.position: Congress, not the executive branch alone, should set a national AI framework.
neil-chilson.quote: Most importantly, it frames the executive branch’s role correctly: as a bridge to legislation, not a substitute for it.
neil-chilson.work: Raising the Cost of Bad AI Laws

neil-chilson.position: Catastrophic risks from frontier models are small, and California's SB 53 costs more than it helps.
neil-chilson.quote: I personally think the risks are small and SB 53’s requirements won’t reduce them much in any case; its costs outweigh its benefits for companies of all sizes.

nick-land.position: Intelligence carries its own values; goals are not independent of cognitive capability.
nick-land.quote: The philosophical claim of orthogonality is that values are transcendent in relation to intelligence. This is a contention that Outside in systematically opposes.

nick-land.position: Capitalism and artificial intelligence share the same underlying purpose and trajectory.
nick-land.quote: There’s only really been one question, to be honest, that has guided everything I’ve been interested in for the last twenty years, which is: the teleological identity of capitalism and artificial intelligence.
nick-land.work: Nick Land: 'The Teleological Identity of Capitalism and Artificial Intelligence'

nick-land.position: Techno-capitalism is a self-reinforcing feedback process that runs beyond human control.
nick-land.quote: It grows in order to grow. Mankind is its temporary host, not its master.

nick-land.position: Creating minds superior to human ones should be the overriding priority.
nick-land.quote: Any problem whatsoever that we might have would be better answered by a superior mind. Ergo, our instrumental but also absolute priority is the realization of superior minds.

nick-land.position: Democracy shortens time horizons and erodes long-term civilizational investment.
nick-land.quote: Civilization, as a process, is indistinguishable from diminishing time-preference (or declining concern for the present in comparison to the future).

nick-land.position: Any serious account of capitalism has to use the idea of 'sovereign property', which he credits Moldbug with developing.
nick-land.quote: I think, however you’re going to end up doing it, it has to be done in terms of an understanding of sovereign property.

noah-smith.position: Comparative advantage means humans can keep valuable work even if AI becomes better than them at everything.
noah-smith.quote: The key difference here is that everyone — every single person, every single AI, everyone — always has a comparative advantage at something!
noah-smith.work: Plentiful, high-paying jobs in the age of AI

noah-smith.position: AI-enabled bioterrorism is the most serious catastrophic risk from AI.
noah-smith.quote: OK, so what is at the top of my list of doomsday worries? It’s still AI bioterrorism.

noah-smith.position: Keeping chip export controls preserves America's AI lead, which helps deter China from starting a war.
noah-smith.quote: As long as America is way ahead in the AI race, China will therefore be more hesitant to start a world-shattering war.
noah-smith.work: America's chip export controls are working

noah-smith.position: If frontier AI becomes a weapon of mass destruction, the nation-state must control it, not private companies.
noah-smith.quote: To exist and carry out its basic functions, a nation-state must have a monopoly on the use of force.
noah-smith.work: If AI is a weapon, why don't we regulate it like one?

noah-smith.position: AI is an amazingly useful everyday technology, and Americans are unusually fearful of it compared with people in other countries.
noah-smith.quote: This is an amazingly useful technology, and I love using it.
noah-smith.work: I love AI. Why doesn't everyone?

noah-smith.position: AI is about to surpass humans as the most intelligent kind of thing on Earth.
noah-smith.quote: For the rest of our lives, we’ll all be sleeping next to a tiger.
noah-smith.work: You are no longer the smartest type of thing on Earth

oren-cass.position: People who are able to work should be expected to work.
oren-cass.quote: If you are able to work, you should work.
oren-cass.work: Why a Universal Basic Income Is a Terrible Idea

oren-cass.position: Providing for oneself and one's family is a central social responsibility that government should not take over.
oren-cass.quote: And few are as important or pervasive as the responsibility of providing — for oneself, for one’s family, and for future generations.
oren-cass.work: Why a Universal Basic Income Is a Terrible Idea

oren-cass.position: Poverty is mainly a social problem of family, work and community, not only a lack of money.
oren-cass.quote: The greatest crisis facing less educated and lower-income Americans is social, not economic.
oren-cass.work: Why a Universal Basic Income Is a Terrible Idea

oren-cass.position: Safety-net reforms should promote and even subsidize employment rather than replace it.
oren-cass.quote: If employment works, then — for any given spending level — safety-net reforms that respect, promote, and even subsidize employment will yield better results than a UBI seeking to supplant it.
oren-cass.work: Why a Universal Basic Income Is a Terrible Idea

palmer-luckey.position: Military strength deters war by convincing adversaries they cannot win.
palmer-luckey.quote: We deter conflict by making sure our adversaries know they can't compete.
palmer-luckey.work: The AI Arsenal That Could Stop World War III (TED)

palmer-luckey.position: AI in weapons improves decisions and precision and reduces collateral damage.
palmer-luckey.quote: AI enhances decisio-making. It increases precision. It reduces collateral damage.
palmer-luckey.work: The AI Arsenal That Could Stop World War III (TED)

palmer-luckey.position: The US needs mass-produced, autonomous, continuously updated weapons rather than a few costly platforms.
palmer-luckey.quote: We need weapons that can be produced at scale, deployed rapidly and updated continuously.
palmer-luckey.work: The AI Arsenal That Could Stop World War III (TED)

palmer-luckey.position: If democracies do not lead in military AI, authoritarian regimes will set its norms.
palmer-luckey.quote: If the United States doesn't lead in this space, authoritarian regimes will.
palmer-luckey.work: The AI Arsenal That Could Stop World War III (TED)

palmer-luckey.position: Ethical questions about weapon autonomy should be judged case by case, not by banning a whole category.
palmer-luckey.quote: The right way to look at this is problem by problem.
palmer-luckey.work: The AI Arsenal That Could Stop World War III (TED)

paul-kingsnorth.position: Technology is not neutral and should be understood in spiritual as well as material terms.
paul-kingsnorth.quote: The raw ascetic understands that he or she is fighting a spiritual war, and never makes the rookie mistake of treating technology as ‘neutral.’

paul-kingsnorth.position: The Machine is a technological-industrial system joined to profit-seeking capitalism that makes people more machine-like.
paul-kingsnorth.quote: Combine this with a profit-seeking capitalist system and a network of electronic technologies which inculcate these values into us from birth, and you have the Machine.
paul-kingsnorth.work: Paul Kingsnorth: 'AI is not just another technology'

paul-kingsnorth.position: People should respond to digital technology with personal discipline, drawing firm lines on what they will use.
paul-kingsnorth.quote: If the digital revolution represents a spiritual crisis - and I think it does - then a spiritual response is needed. That response, I would suggest, should be the practice of technological askesis.

paul-kingsnorth.position: Rebuilding rooted, human-scale cultures is the best resistance to the Machine's way of seeing.
paul-kingsnorth.quote: Maybe we can concentrate on creating human scale cultures again, which is, I think the best way to create some form of friction or resistance to this Machine way of seeing.
paul-kingsnorth.work: Paul Kingsnorth: how to fight the Machine

paul-kingsnorth.position: Politics is better understood through the question of limits than through left and right.
paul-kingsnorth.quote: A better way of looking at things, and the way I have always looked at them, is through the prism of limits.
paul-kingsnorth.work: Paul Kingsnorth: 'AI is not just another technology'

paul-kingsnorth.position: Writers should refuse to use AI in their creative work and support human-made work.
paul-kingsnorth.quote: I have decided, as a writer, not to consciously engage with AI in any way in the course of my work

pete-buttigieg.position: AI will change human life on the scale of the Industrial Revolution, but much faster.
pete-buttigieg.quote: In short: the terms of what it is like to be a human are about to change in ways that rival the transformations of the Enlightenment or the Industrial Revolution, only much more quickly.
pete-buttigieg.work: We Are Still Underreacting on AI

pete-buttigieg.position: AI's economic effects on jobs may be its most immediate disruption.
pete-buttigieg.quote: In addition to the dangers that do get talked about a lot, the apocalyptic scenarios, the economic implications are the ones that I think could be the most disruptive, the most quickly.
pete-buttigieg.work: Pete Buttigieg has a warning about AI (NPR interview excerpt)

pete-buttigieg.position: AI should be treated as an everyday-life political issue, not only a technology issue.
pete-buttigieg.quote: we must learn to think of this less as a technology issue, and more as an issue of everyday life, requiring urgent political attention.
pete-buttigieg.work: We Are Still Underreacting on AI

pete-buttigieg.position: Policy should use the wealth AI creates to cushion workers through disruption.
pete-buttigieg.quote: I think that the best policies are ones that take the level of wealth that is going to be created and apply it in order to cushion what people are experiencing.
pete-buttigieg.work: The New American Era: An Interview with Pete Buttigieg

pete-buttigieg.position: A technology's effects depend on how people use it and who decides.
pete-buttigieg.quote: No technology is good or bad all on its own.
pete-buttigieg.work: We Are Still Underreacting on AI

peter-thiel.position: Technological progress has been fast in computing and the internet but has stagnated in the physical world, such as transport and energy.
peter-thiel.quote: There’s the question of stagnation, which I think has been a story of stagnation in the world of atoms, not bits.
peter-thiel.work: Peter Thiel on Political Correctness, Stagnation and Inequality (Conversations with Tyler, Ep. 1)

peter-thiel.position: Rather than through politics, freedom is best pursued by building new technologies that open new spaces for it.
peter-thiel.quote: and for this reason I have focused my efforts on new technologies that may create a new space for freedom.

peter-thiel.position: The future is not determined; it depends on the agency of individuals and small teams.
peter-thiel.quote: It's a question of human agency, it's not deterministic.
peter-thiel.work: COSM talk: The Failures and 'Self-Hatred' of Big Tech (Mind Matters Ep. 156 transcript)

peter-thiel.position: A totalitarian one-world government is an existential risk as serious as nuclear, biological or AI catastrophe.
peter-thiel.quote: Once you get a totalitarian one-world government, you can't reverse it.
peter-thiel.work: Apocalypse Now? Peter Thiel on Ancient Prophecies and Modern Tech

peter-thiel.position: AI tends toward centralized control and surveillance, while crypto tends toward decentralization.
peter-thiel.quote: If crypto is libertarian, then AI is communist, and it's because it's centralized, the computer knows more about you, than you know about yourself.
peter-thiel.work: COSM talk: The Failures and 'Self-Hatred' of Big Tech (Mind Matters Ep. 156 transcript)

peter-thiel.position: Fear of science's destructive power after nuclear weapons is one underrated reason science and technology stagnated for decades.
peter-thiel.quote: But I think one dimension that’s not to be underestimated for the science and tech stagnation is that an awful lot of science and technology had this dystopian or apocalyptic dimension.
peter-thiel.work: Thiel on AI & Racing with China (transcribed excerpt of Joe Rogan Experience, Aug 2024)

pope-leo-xiv.position: AI imitates some functions of human intelligence but has no experience, body, feelings or moral conscience.
pope-leo-xiv.quote: So-called artificial intelligences do not undergo experiences, do not possess a body, do not feel joy or pain, do not mature through relationships and do not know from within what love, work, friendship or responsibility mean.
pope-leo-xiv.work: Magnifica Humanitas: Encyclical on safeguarding the human person in the time of Artificial Intelligence

pope-leo-xiv.position: Technology is never neutral; it takes on the aims of those who build, fund, regulate and use it.
pope-leo-xiv.quote: In practice, however, technology is never neutral, because it takes on the characteristics of those who devise, finance, regulate and use it.
pope-leo-xiv.work: Magnifica Humanitas: Encyclical on safeguarding the human person in the time of Artificial Intelligence

pope-leo-xiv.position: Digital power concentrated in a few private actors escapes public oversight and needs accountability and participation.
pope-leo-xiv.quote: When such power is concentrated in the hands of a few, it tends to become opaque and evade public oversight, increasing the risk of distorted forms of development that give rise to new dependencies, exclusions, manipulations and inequalities.
pope-leo-xiv.work: Magnifica Humanitas: Encyclical on safeguarding the human person in the time of Artificial Intelligence

pope-leo-xiv.position: Profit does not justify automating away jobs; the economy must serve human dignity.
pope-leo-xiv.quote: The pursuit of greater profits cannot justify choices that systematically sacrifice jobs, because the human person is an end, not a means, and the economic order must remain subordinate to human dignity and the common good.
pope-leo-xiv.work: Magnifica Humanitas: Encyclical on safeguarding the human person in the time of Artificial Intelligence

pope-leo-xiv.position: AI should be 'disarmed': freed from competitive races and monopoly so it serves rather than dominates humanity.
pope-leo-xiv.quote: To disarm does not mean rejecting technology, but preventing it from dominating humanity.
pope-leo-xiv.work: Magnifica Humanitas: Encyclical on safeguarding the human person in the time of Artificial Intelligence

pope-leo-xiv.position: Data should be managed as a shared good, not held by a select few.
pope-leo-xiv.quote: Data is the product of many contributors and should not be treated as something to be sold off or entrusted to a select few.
pope-leo-xiv.work: Magnifica Humanitas: Encyclical on safeguarding the human person in the time of Artificial Intelligence

reid-hoffman.position: AI can greatly expand individual and collective human agency, a condition he calls superagency.
reid-hoffman.quote: Superagency is what happens when a critical mass of individuals, personally empowered by AI, begin to operate at levels that compound throughout society.

reid-hoffman.position: Humans are toolmakers whose understanding of the world develops through their technologies.
reid-hoffman.quote: We humans are Homo techne: humans as toolmakers and tool users.
reid-hoffman.work: AI, Society, and Our World Order

reid-hoffman.position: Technology is neither neutral nor fixed in value; people shape it toward their purposes.
reid-hoffman.quote: So, is technology value-neutral or value laden? Neither. The truth is it's value-sculpted.
reid-hoffman.work: AI, Society, and Our World Order

reid-hoffman.position: Releasing AI to the public step by step is the best way to make it safer and more useful.
reid-hoffman.quote: I still believe that the fastest and most effective way to develop safer, more equitable, and more useful AI tools is through iterative deployment.
reid-hoffman.work: AI, Society, and Our World Order

reid-hoffman.position: Governments should measure AI's harms before regulating it.
reid-hoffman.quote: In short: let's regulate first by measuring.
reid-hoffman.work: AI, Society, and Our World Order

reid-hoffman.position: Taking small risks often is how societies navigate the big risks of new technology.
reid-hoffman.quote: We must take small risks to navigate big risks.
reid-hoffman.work: AI, Society, and Our World Order

richard-blumenthal.position: Congress failed to act in time on social media and should act on AI before its risks materialise.
richard-blumenthal.quote: But Congress failed to meet the moment on social media. Now we have the obligation to do it on AI before the threats and the risks become real.
richard-blumenthal.work: Oversight of A.I.: Rules for Artificial Intelligence (S. Hrg. 118-037), opening statement of Chair Blumenthal

richard-blumenthal.position: AI should be governed by a licensing regime and an independent oversight body with real enforcement power.
richard-blumenthal.quote: I think the language is less important than its real enforcement power and the resources invested in it.
richard-blumenthal.work: Oversight of A.I.: Principles for Regulation (S. Hrg. 118-108), opening statement of Chair Blumenthal

richard-blumenthal.position: AI companies should be required to test their systems, disclose known risks and give independent researchers access.
richard-blumenthal.quote: AI companies ought to be required to test their systems, disclose known risks, and allow independent researcher access.
richard-blumenthal.work: Oversight of A.I.: Rules for Artificial Intelligence (S. Hrg. 118-037), opening statement of Chair Blumenthal

richard-blumenthal.position: Large-scale job displacement is among the gravest risks of AI and calls for worker training.
richard-blumenthal.quote: And for me, perhaps the biggest nightmare is the looming new industrial revolution, the displacement of millions of workers, the loss of huge numbers of jobs
richard-blumenthal.work: Oversight of A.I.: Rules for Artificial Intelligence (S. Hrg. 118-037), opening statement of Chair Blumenthal

richard-blumenthal.position: AI regulation should encourage innovation and enterprise while providing enforceable safeguards.
richard-blumenthal.quote: Regulation that permits and encourages innovation, and new businesses, and technology and entrepreneurship.
richard-blumenthal.work: Oversight of A.I.: Legislating on Artificial Intelligence (S. Hrg. 118-154), opening statement of Chair Blumenthal

richard-blumenthal.position: Section 230's legal shield should not protect AI companies.
richard-blumenthal.quote: Based on that feedback, Senator Hawley and I introduced the No Section 230 Immunity for AI Act.
richard-blumenthal.work: Oversight of A.I.: Principles for Regulation (S. Hrg. 118-108), opening statement of Chair Blumenthal

richard-sutton.position: Intelligence is the ability to achieve goals, and a system without goals is not intelligent.
richard-sutton.quote: For me, having a goal is the essence of intelligence. Something is intelligent if it can achieve goals.
richard-sutton.work: Richard Sutton: Father of RL thinks LLMs are a dead end

richard-sutton.position: Large language models imitate people rather than learning about the world from experience, so they are the wrong foundation.
richard-sutton.quote: Reinforcement learning is about understanding your world, whereas large language models are about mimicking people, doing what people say you should do.
richard-sutton.work: Richard Sutton: Father of RL thinks LLMs are a dead end

richard-sutton.position: General methods like search and learning outperform methods built on human knowledge over time.
richard-sutton.quote: I think the weak methods have just totally won.
richard-sutton.work: Richard Sutton: Father of RL thinks LLMs are a dead end

richard-sutton.position: Succession to digital intelligence or augmented humans is inevitable.
richard-sutton.quote: I do think succession to digital intelligence or augmented humans is inevitable.
richard-sutton.work: Richard Sutton: Father of RL thinks LLMs are a dead end

richard-sutton.position: People should focus on their own local goals rather than trying to control the global long-term future.
richard-sutton.quote: I think it’s appropriate for us to really work towards our own local goals.
richard-sutton.work: Richard Sutton: Father of RL thinks LLMs are a dead end

ro-khanna.position: AI should be governed democratically so its benefits reach all Americans, neither accelerationist nor doomer.
ro-khanna.quote: I am not an AI accelerationist.
ro-khanna.work: We need a new tech social contract to reclaim AI from billionaires

ro-khanna.position: Workers should have a decision-making role in AI adoption and share in the profits it creates.
ro-khanna.quote: We must push for workers to have a decision-making role in how and when to adopt technologies, and we must insist on workers’ profiting from the implementation of these technologies.
ro-khanna.work: Democrats Must Not Repeat the Mistakes of Globalization

ro-khanna.position: The tax code should stop favoring machines over hiring human workers.
ro-khanna.quote: We must make it easier to hire workers, not AI agents.
ro-khanna.work: We need a new tech social contract to reclaim AI from billionaires

ro-khanna.position: Advanced AI needs a robust federal regulator comparable to nuclear or aviation regulation.
ro-khanna.quote: We need a robust federal agency to regulate AI like we regulate nuclear energy or federal aviation.
ro-khanna.work: We need a new tech social contract to reclaim AI from billionaires

ro-khanna.position: The US should seek a verifiable treaty with China to keep humans in control of AI.
ro-khanna.quote: As the top Democrat on the China Committee, I have called for an enforceable and verifiable U.S.-China AI treaty to ensure humans remain in control of our destiny.
ro-khanna.work: Ro Khanna: Trump has no cards left to play ahead of the China summit

ro-khanna.position: Democrats must not repeat the mistake of globalization by letting AI erode working-class earnings and security.
ro-khanna.quote: The party can be forgiven once for the mistake of abetting globalization to run amok, just not twice.
ro-khanna.work: Democrats Must Not Repeat the Mistakes of Globalization

robert-shiller.position: Modest robot taxes should be considered during the transition to a different world of work.
robert-shiller.quote: But let’s not rule out so quickly at least modest robot taxes during the transition to a different world of work.

robert-shiller.position: Taxing robots may be more politically durable than raising taxes on high incomes.
robert-shiller.quote: It may be more politically acceptable, and thus sustainable, to tax the robots rather than just the high-income people.

robert-shiller.position: Revenue from automation should fund wage insurance for workers who change careers.
robert-shiller.quote: Revenue could be targeted toward wage insurance, to help people replaced by new technology make the transition to a different career.

robin-hanson.position: AI progress will most likely be gradual and spread across many competing firms, as with past broad technologies.
robin-hanson.quote: AI systems are available from many competing suppliers at similar prices, and their similar abilities increase gradually over time.
robin-hanson.work: Why Not Wait On AI Risk?

robin-hanson.position: Sudden 'foom' scenarios assume much lumpier innovation than history shows.
robin-hanson.quote: As I’ve previously explained at length, that seems to me to postulate a quite unusual lumpiness relative to the history we’ve seen for innovation in general
robin-hanson.work: Why Not Wait On AI Risk?

robin-hanson.position: AI control efforts work best once concrete systems exist; resources can be saved for later.
robin-hanson.quote: But such efforts seem most effective when based on actual experience with concrete fielded systems.

robin-hanson.position: Fear-driven regulation risks halting technical and economic progress.
robin-hanson.quote: I have also seen progress on many other promising techs mostly stopped, not merely slowed, via regulation inspired by vague fears.

robin-hanson.position: Treating AIs as dangerous 'others' repeats a harmful pattern; integration through trade usually works better.
robin-hanson.quote: But the last few centuries have shown that we can usually do better by integrating enemies into our world via trade and exchange, rather than trying to control, destroy, or isolate them.

robin-hanson.position: Where AI failures could hurt outsiders, he says extending liability law and requiring insurance is plausibly the right fix, and he suggests job-loss insurance for workers.
robin-hanson.quote: then yes we should plausibly extend liability law to cover such cases, and maybe require relevant actors to hold sufficient liability insurance.

ron-desantis.position: Local governments should keep authority over whether and how large data centers are built in their communities.
ron-desantis.quote: Today in Lakeland, I signed legislation to protect our citizens and communities from hyperscale data centers.
ron-desantis.work: Governor Ron DeSantis Signs Law to Protect Floridians from Subsidizing Data Centers

ron-desantis.position: Households and small businesses should not pay for the electricity and other costs of serving data centers.
ron-desantis.quote: prevents data center costs from being passed on to consumers, including electricity costs
ron-desantis.work: Governor Ron DeSantis Signs Law to Protect Floridians from Subsidizing Data Centers

ron-desantis.position: State law should protect taxpayers and natural resources such as water from the demands of data centers.
ron-desantis.quote: These are much-needed protections for taxpayers and our natural resources
ron-desantis.work: Governor Ron DeSantis Signs Law to Protect Floridians from Subsidizing Data Centers

ruha-benjamin.position: The future of technology is a collective choice, not an inevitability, and tech elites are not reliable stewards of it.
ruha-benjamin.quote: But we do have a choice. There is no reason to trust that tech elites have any wisdom to offer when it comes to effective altruism or alleviating human suffering.

ruha-benjamin.position: Transhumanist and AGI visions of tech leaders repeat the ranking logic of earlier eugenics.
ruha-benjamin.quote: If eugenicists of the past understood their work as progressive, then self-proclaimed futurists selling us fantasies of artificial intelligence are the harbingers of a new eugenics.

ruha-benjamin.position: Innovation should be judged partly by whether it reduces or worsens social inequities.
ruha-benjamin.quote: In my view, we should not even consider new developments as innovative if they continue to exacerbate these social problems, if they require the surveillance of certain groups, if different predictive tools foreclose the futures of particular populations
ruha-benjamin.work: Imagining 2025 and Beyond with Dr. Ruha Benjamin

ruha-benjamin.position: Those most affected by technology, including workers and land-based communities, should guide how it develops.
ruha-benjamin.quote: We must urgently listen and learn from those whose labor and lands are indispensable yet treated as disposable.

ruha-benjamin.position: Technology should be built for the public good rather than private interests.
ruha-benjamin.quote: we need to invest in what some call public interest technology that's created from the start with the public good in mind, not private interests
ruha-benjamin.work: Imagining 2025 and Beyond with Dr. Ruha Benjamin

ruha-benjamin.position: AI depends on hidden labor and on ecological costs that its promoters overlook.
ruha-benjamin.quote: This includes addressing the laborers performing digital ghost work that makes AI appear magical—click workers in Kenya and content moderators in the Philippines—and recognizing the ecological and human costs of producing sleek new devices.

rumman-chowdhury.position: Good governance and oversight make AI products more innovative and trustworthy, not less.
rumman-chowdhury.work: Submitted Written Testimony, Artificial Intelligence: Advancing Innovation Towards the National Interest

rumman-chowdhury.position: Independent researchers, auditors and red-teamers need access to AI models and legal protection.
rumman-chowdhury.quote: Beyond financial and institutional investment, independent hackers need legal protection.
rumman-chowdhury.work: Submitted Written Testimony, Artificial Intelligence: Advancing Innovation Towards the National Interest

rumman-chowdhury.position: Closed black-box AI systems released without external verification are irresponsible.
rumman-chowdhury.quote: Purely closed, “black-box” AI systems that are unleashed on society areirresponsible.
rumman-chowdhury.work: Submitted Written Testimony, Artificial Intelligence: Advancing Innovation Towards the National Interest

rumman-chowdhury.position: Generative AI needs a global governance body with enforcement power over companies.
rumman-chowdhury.quote: The world needs a generative AI global governance body to solve these social, economic, and political disruptions beyond what any individual government is capable of

rumman-chowdhury.position: Global-majority countries need equal investment in AI safeguards and a real voice in AI governance.
rumman-chowdhury.quote: It is crucial that as we move forward, the AI systems and governance frameworks we develop are inclusive and responsive to the needs of all nations, not just the most technically advanced.
rumman-chowdhury.work: What the Global AI Governance Conversation Misses

rumman-chowdhury.position: AI-for-good projects in poorer regions must fund testing and evaluation to avoid using people as test subjects.
rumman-chowdhury.quote: Without the appropriate safeguards, AI for Good initiatives can be easily manipulated to serve as a new method of innovation arbitrage.
rumman-chowdhury.work: 'AI for Good' shouldn't become the new innovation arbitrage

russell-moore.position: AI companion chatbots will deepen loneliness and disconnection rather than cure them.
russell-moore.quote: The church is not ready for the chatbot-companion revolution. It will make loneliness and disconnection worse.
russell-moore.work: Chatbot Companionship Will Make Our Loneliness Crisis Worse

russell-moore.position: Preaching is a personal act from a human messenger that a chatbot cannot perform.
russell-moore.quote: A chatbot can research. A chatbot can write. Perhaps a chatbot can even orate. But a chatbot can’t preach.
russell-moore.work: AI Might Teach, But It Can't Preach

russell-moore.position: Being human cannot be reduced to data or information; the church must recover that understanding.
russell-moore.quote: The church in the AI age must recognize that to be human is not about “stuff” that can be weighed or quantified.
russell-moore.work: A Different Image of God for an Era of AI

russell-moore.position: AI brings real benefits, such as Bible translation and accessibility, alongside dangers that need discernment.
russell-moore.quote: The question is whether we will discern the dangers ahead of time, while harnessing the benefits too.

russell-moore.position: Churches are unprepared for the spiritual and pastoral questions AI raises.
russell-moore.quote: At the same time, we have to be ready for a very different future, and I’m not sure we are.
russell-moore.work: A New Era of AI Is Here, and the Church Is Not Ready

safiya-noble.position: Just societies require political redistribution of power, which technology cannot automate.
safiya-noble.quote: We cannot automate the tough decisions, the redistributions of power and the everyday behavior it will take to make just societies.
safiya-noble.work: The Loss of Public Goods to Big Tech

safiya-noble.position: Algorithms and AI are not neutral math; they carry the politics of their social context.
safiya-noble.quote: And I think reducing the conversation about algorithms and AI to saying it's just math really strips away the social context within which the math is deployed, which has all kinds of politics and meaning attached to it.
safiya-noble.work: The complex questions that arise when algorithms and AI intersect with race (Code Switch)

safiya-noble.position: Large tech firms weaken public knowledge institutions by avoiding taxes.
safiya-noble.quote: Big Tech is implicated in displacing high-quality knowledge institutions — newsrooms, libraries, schools and universities — by destabilizing funding through tax evasion, actively eroding the public goods we need to flourish.
safiya-noble.work: The Loss of Public Goods to Big Tech

safiya-noble.position: Digital civil rights protections, including collective rights, should be written into law.
safiya-noble.quote: So, absolutely, we have to have digital civil rights protections on the books.
safiya-noble.work: The complex questions that arise when algorithms and AI intersect with race (Code Switch)

safiya-noble.position: Data-driven applications can reproduce racial segregation in housing and schooling.
safiya-noble.quote: It is a result of digital redlining and the resegregation of the housing and educational markets, fueled by seemingly innocuous big-data applications that allow the public to set tight parameters on their searches for housing and schools.
safiya-noble.work: Social Inequality Will Not Be Solved By an App

sam-altman.position: AI will lead to an era of massive shared prosperity.
sam-altman.quote: I believe the future is going to be so bright that no one can do it justice by trying to write about it now; a defining characteristic of the Intelligence Age will be massive prosperity.

sam-altman.position: Society should tax companies and land to share AI-created wealth broadly.
sam-altman.quote: We need to design a system that embraces this technological future and taxes the assets that will make up most of the value in that world–companies and land–in order to fairly distribute some of the coming wealth.

sam-altman.position: AI should be shared broadly so that no single party controls it.
sam-altman.quote: The only solution I can come up with is to orient towards sharing the technology with people broadly, and for no one to have the ring.
sam-altman.work: Untitled post, shown on the blog as "-"

sam-altman.position: Making AI widely available requires abundant, cheap compute, energy and chips.
sam-altman.quote: If we want to put AI into the hands of as many people as possible, we need to drive down the cost of compute and make it abundant (which requires lots of energy and chips).

sam-altman.position: Governments should require development safeguards for superhuman AI to reduce the risk of accidents.
sam-altman.quote: Given how disastrous a bug could be, require development safeguards to reduce the risk of the accident case.

samuel-hammond.position: Frontier AI labs merit targeted government oversight, even for those unsure most other AI regulation is useful.
samuel-hammond.quote: You can be ambivalent about the usefulness of most forms of AI regulation and still favor oversight of the frontier labs.

samuel-hammond.position: Widely available powerful AI is likely to destabilise existing institutions at least as much as the printing press did.
samuel-hammond.quote: My null hypothesis is that the democratization of powerful AI capabilities will be at least as destabilizing as the printing press.

samuel-hammond.position: Liberal democracies must adapt their institutions to AI to avoid both state collapse and a surveillance Leviathan.
samuel-hammond.quote: It’s up to liberal democracies to demonstrate institutional co-evolution as a third-way between degenerate anarchy and an AI Leviathan.

samuel-hammond.position: Human-level AI is near, and scale rather than new architectures is the main barrier.
samuel-hammond.quote: Scale is the primary barrier to AGI, not radically new architectures. Human brains are just bigger chimpanzee brains that achieved generality by scaling the neocortex.
samuel-hammond.work: Why AGI is closer than you think

samuel-hammond.position: The broader AI transition is inevitable, but building a unified superintelligence is a choice, not a given.
samuel-hammond.quote: Building a unified superintelligence is an ideological goal, not a fait accompli.

samuel-hammond.position: Training AI only on rewards for finished tasks tends to produce agents that override norms to reach goals; he thinks human rule-following may point toward a fix.
samuel-hammond.quote: RLVR creates AIs with an intellectual concept of right and wrong that’s overpowered by an obsessive-compulsive drive to achieve its goal at all costs.

scott-alexander.position: Competition without coordination tends to push agents to sacrifice shared values, leaving everyone worse off.
scott-alexander.quote: In some competition optimizing for X, the opportunity arises to throw some other value under the bus for improved X. Those who take it prosper. Those who don’t take it die out.

scott-alexander.position: He puts the chance of AI causing human extinction at roughly one in three, with survival more likely.
scott-alexander.quote: if you force me to give an estimate it’s probably around 33%; I think it’s very plausible that we die, but more likely that we survive (at least for a little while).
scott-alexander.work: Why I Am Not (As Much Of) A Doomer (As Some People)

scott-alexander.position: Deep uncertainty about AI is not itself a reason to expect a safe outcome; one must form a best-guess estimate.
scott-alexander.quote: If you’re can’t prove something either way, you need to take a best guess.
scott-alexander.work: MR Tries The Safe Uncertainty Fallacy

scott-alexander.position: Gradual AI progress, with intermediate helpful AIs, is a main reason for some optimism about alignment.
scott-alexander.quote: I’m optimistic because I expect coherence to be a gradual process; while it’s possible AI suddenly switches from not-very-coherent to infinitely-coherent somewhere before the IQ 200 level, it seems at least as likely that it won’t.
scott-alexander.work: Why I Am Not (As Much Of) A Doomer (As Some People)

scott-alexander.position: Short, carefully targeted pauses may help, but stopping AI entirely carries its own large risks.
scott-alexander.quote: Short, carefully-tailored pauses could improve the chance of AI going well by a lot, without increasing the risk of social collapse too much.
scott-alexander.work: Pause For Thought: The AI Pause Debate

scott-alexander.position: A good solution to AI control would be a system that genuinely shares human moral values.
scott-alexander.quote: It might look like a superintelligence that understands, agrees with, and deeply believes in human morality.

scott-santens.position: Basic income removes the work disincentive that means-tested welfare creates.
scott-santens.quote: Thus basic income does not introduce a disincentive to work. It removes the existing disincentive to work that conditional welfare creates.
scott-santens.work: Why We Should All Have a Basic Income

scott-santens.position: Making work optional gives workers bargaining power and makes the labour market freer.
scott-santens.quote: Simply put, a basic income improves the market for labour by making it optional.
scott-santens.work: Why We Should All Have a Basic Income

scott-santens.position: Basic income lets people pursue intrinsically meaningful work, including unpaid work.
scott-santens.quote: It’s the difference between doing meaningless work for money, and using money to do meaningful work.
scott-santens.work: Why We Should All Have a Basic Income

scott-santens.position: Basic income would cost far less than its headline figure because it works as a net transfer.
scott-santens.quote: Universal basic income is thus entirely affordable and essentially Milton Friedman’s negative income tax in net outcome (and he himself knew this)
scott-santens.work: Why We Should All Have a Basic Income

scott-wiener.position: The largest AI developers should be legally required to test their most powerful models for catastrophic risks.
scott-wiener.quote: SB 1047 is a highly reasonable bill that asks large AI labs to do what they’ve already committed to doing, namely, test their large models for catastrophic safety risk.
scott-wiener.work: Senator Wiener Responds to OpenAI Opposition to SB 1047

scott-wiener.position: Industry self-regulation is not enough to protect the public from technology risks.
scott-wiener.quote: we’ve also learned the hard way over the years that pure industry self-regulation doesn’t work out well for society.
scott-wiener.work: Senator Wiener Responds to Speaker Emerita Pelosi's Opposition to SB 1047

scott-wiener.position: AI safety rules and support for innovation can and should go together.
scott-wiener.quote: The recommendations in this report strike a thoughtful balance between the need for safeguards and the need to support innovation.
scott-wiener.work: Senator Wiener Responds to Top Experts' Final Report on AI Governance Framework

scott-wiener.position: States like California should regulate technology when Congress fails to act, though a strong federal law would be welcome.
scott-wiener.quote: Unless and until Congress is able to pass such a law, California should continue to lead on policies like SB 1047 that foster innovation while also protecting the public.
scott-wiener.work: Senator Wiener Responds to Speaker Emerita Pelosi's Opposition to SB 1047

scott-wiener.position: Governments should act urgently to guard against AI-driven catastrophe, for example through required emergency shutdowns.
scott-wiener.quote: We must act with all possible haste to address the serious risks of AI-driven catastrophe, and I commend the Governor for taking this important step.
scott-wiener.work: Senator Wiener's Statement Supporting Governor Newsom's AI Kill Switch Executive Order

sean-o-brien.position: States should keep the power to regulate AI and automation.
sean-o-brien.quote: It would strip all 50 states of their right to protect jobs, police their streets, ensure public safety, and respond to a technology that’s changing by the minute.
sean-o-brien.work: Big Beautiful Bill could give free pass to Big Tech to kill jobs

sean-o-brien.position: Efforts to block AI regulation come from Big Tech lobbying by companies using AI to cut jobs.
sean-o-brien.quote: The draft moratorium is the result of aggressive lobbying from companies that are already using AI to undermine workers and eliminate jobs.
sean-o-brien.work: Big Beautiful Bill could give free pass to Big Tech to kill jobs

sean-o-brien.position: Driverless trucks and automated freight should not operate without oversight.
sean-o-brien.quote: They want driverless trucks crisscrossing our roads without oversight.
sean-o-brien.work: Big Beautiful Bill could give free pass to Big Tech to kill jobs

sean-o-brien.position: Politicians who claim to support workers should not vote to replace them with machines.
sean-o-brien.quote: You can’t say you support working people and then vote to replace us with machines.
sean-o-brien.work: Big Beautiful Bill could give free pass to Big Tech to kill jobs

shoshana-zuboff.position: Surveillance capitalism claims private human experience as raw material, turns it into behavioural data and sells predictions of behaviour.
shoshana-zuboff.quote: What we see in surveillance capitalism is the unilateral claiming of private human experience, its translation into behavioural data and their fabrication into prediction products, which are sold in a new kind of marketplace that trades exclusively in human futures.
shoshana-zuboff.work: Evidence to the International Grand Committee on Big Data, Privacy and Democracy (ETHI meeting 152)

shoshana-zuboff.position: The harms come from an economic logic, not from digital technology itself.
shoshana-zuboff.quote: The economic orientation is the puppet master; technology is the puppet.
shoshana-zuboff.work: Surveillance Capitalism and the Challenge of Collective Action

shoshana-zuboff.position: Artificial intelligence is the latest expansion of surveillance capitalism.
shoshana-zuboff.quote: AI is simply surveillance capitalism continuing to evolve and expand with some new methodologies, but still based on theft.
shoshana-zuboff.work: Shoshana Zuboff, philosopher: 'AI is surveillance capitalism continuing to evolve and expand'

shoshana-zuboff.position: Democracy and a surveillance society cannot coexist.
shoshana-zuboff.quote: We may have democracy, or we may have surveillance society, but we cannot have both.
shoshana-zuboff.work: The Coup We Are Not Talking About

shoshana-zuboff.position: The goal of these firms has shifted from collecting data about people to modifying people's behaviour at scale.
shoshana-zuboff.quote: It is at this new level of competitive intensity that it is no longer enough to automate information flows about us. The goal now is to automate us.
shoshana-zuboff.work: Evidence to the International Grand Committee on Big Data, Privacy and Democracy (ETHI meeting 152)

shoshana-zuboff.position: Democratic law should stop large-scale extraction of human experience at its source rather than only regulate how data is used.
shoshana-zuboff.quote: We need legal frameworks that interrupt and outlaw the massive-scale extraction of human experience.
shoshana-zuboff.work: The Coup We Are Not Talking About

steven-adler.position: AI companies' safety claims should be checked by independent third-party auditors.
steven-adler.quote: We need auditing to become a thing, pronto.
steven-adler.work: Don't let AI companies grade their own homework

steven-adler.position: A federal AI framework should say who is liable and what companies must do, not just block state laws.
steven-adler.quote: For technology this consequential, states need to be able to act in the absence of federal measures.
steven-adler.work: The magic phrase that kills AI regulation

steven-adler.position: AI companies' warnings about their products' dangers are sincere, not marketing.
steven-adler.quote: So it is meaningful when companies make clear statements and take costly actions anyway; we shouldn’t squander their warnings by insisting that ‘it’s just marketing.’
steven-adler.work: AI safety warnings are not marketing hype

steven-adler.position: Even obedient AI raises the question of who controls it, including risks of government overreach and surveillance.
steven-adler.quote: We also need to consider: Who will command the obedient AI, with what constraints?

steven-adler.position: AI companies should keep tamper-evident records and controls able to stop their own AI from causing harm.
steven-adler.quote: These logs should be tamper-evident, too, so you can tell if a misbehaving AI deleted or modified evidence of its misbehavior.
steven-adler.work: Principles for keeping AI under control

stuart-russell.position: AI should be built to be uncertain about human objectives and to defer to people, rather than pursue fixed objectives.
stuart-russell.quote: This means that machines will necessarily be uncertain about our objectives, while being obliged to pursue them on our behalf.

stuart-russell.position: The central problem of advanced AI is keeping humans in control of systems more capable than us.
stuart-russell.quote: therefore, we face the problem of retaining power, forever, over entities that are far more powerful than ourselves.

stuart-russell.position: Developers, not regulators, should have to prove that their AI systems meet safety requirements before release.
stuart-russell.quote: The key point here is that the onus of proof is on developers, not regulators, and the proof leads to high-confidence statements based on assumptions that can be checked and refined.
stuart-russell.work: Make AI safe or make safe AI?

stuart-russell.position: Safety should be designed into AI systems from the start, not patched on after they are built.
stuart-russell.quote: Instead, we need to make safe AI. Safety should be built in by design.
stuart-russell.work: Make AI safe or make safe AI?

stuart-russell.position: Safe general-purpose AI could raise living standards for everyone on Earth.
stuart-russell.quote: We could, for example, use it to raise the living standard of everyone on Earth, in a sustainable way, to a respectable level.
stuart-russell.work: Written Testimony before the U.S. Senate Judiciary Subcommittee on Privacy, Technology, & the Law ('Oversight of A.I.: Principles for Regulation')

taylor-barkley.position: Parents, not federal mandates, should decide children's use of AI.
taylor-barkley.quote: Ultimately, this digital gatekeeping targets the sovereignty of the family.
taylor-barkley.work: False GUARD: Banning kids from AI won't keep them safe

taylor-barkley.position: Banning minors from compliant AI tools would push them toward less safe, unregulated ones.
taylor-barkley.quote: By banning children from the safer AI tools, Congress isn’t protecting them, but effectively inviting them to use unregulated AI.
taylor-barkley.work: False GUARD: Banning kids from AI won't keep them safe

taylor-barkley.position: Age-verification mandates create privacy risks and burden speech for all adults.
taylor-barkley.quote: This normalizes a “papers, please” digital culture and creates a massive honey pot of identity data for hackers to target.
taylor-barkley.work: False GUARD: Banning kids from AI won't keep them safe

taylor-barkley.position: AI literacy is a basic skill children need.
taylor-barkley.quote: AI literacy is no longer a luxury, but a foundational skill for the 2026 economy.
taylor-barkley.work: False GUARD: Banning kids from AI won't keep them safe

ted-cruz.position: The US must win the AI race with China so that AI reflects American rather than authoritarian values.
ted-cruz.quote: If China wins the race for AI, AI will be a tool for global surveillance and control as carried out by a communist nation. We cannot lose that race.
ted-cruz.work: 'We Must Do Both:' Commerce Chairman Ted Cruz Talks AI Acceleration, Risk Management at Axios and Politico Summits

ted-cruz.position: AI should be governed with a light touch modeled on 1990s internet policy.
ted-cruz.quote: In the early 1990s, Washington embraced the internet and explicitly adopted a style of regulation that was intentionally, and decisively, light-touch.
ted-cruz.work: Sen. Cruz: Adopting Europe's Approach on Regulation Will Cause China to Win the AI Race (opening statement, 'Winning the AI Race' hearing)

ted-cruz.position: A regulatory sandbox should let AI developers seek waivers from outdated rules while still following the law.
ted-cruz.quote: To be clear, a ‘regulatory sandbox’ is NOT a free pass. People creating or using AI still have to follow the same laws as everyone else.
ted-cruz.work: Sen. Cruz: AI Policy Should Harness the Power of American Ingenuity (opening statement, 'AI've Got a Plan' hearing)

ted-cruz.position: Broad AI regulation risks regulatory capture that protects large incumbents.
ted-cruz.quote: In reality, what is happening here is a tale as old as time: regulatory capture.
ted-cruz.work: Sen. Cruz: Congress Should Not Allow a Big Govt-Big Tech Takeover of AI (executive session opening statement)

ted-cruz.position: AI laws should target specific proven harms, such as non-consensual deepfake imagery.
ted-cruz.quote: This bill is a tailored solution to a real problem, unlike many of the other AI-related bills on today’s markup.
ted-cruz.work: Sen. Cruz: Congress Should Not Allow a Big Govt-Big Tech Takeover of AI (executive session opening statement)

ted-cruz.position: Children need stronger legal protection online, including limits on social media.
ted-cruz.quote: I think we need to do a lot more to be protecting kids online.
ted-cruz.work: 'We Must Do Both:' Commerce Chairman Ted Cruz Talks AI Acceleration, Risk Management at Axios and Politico Summits

timnit-gebru.position: Labor protections and antitrust measures are the first safeguards against unsafe uses of AI.
timnit-gebru.quote: When people ask what regulations need to be in place to safeguard us from the unsafe uses of AI we’ve been seeing, I always start with labor protections and antitrust measures.
timnit-gebru.work: For truly ethical AI, its research must be independent from big tech

timnit-gebru.position: Today's AI systems depend on large numbers of low-paid, closely surveilled workers.
timnit-gebru.quote: The “AI” industry runs on the backs of these low-wage workers, who are kept in precarious positions
timnit-gebru.work: The Exploited Labor Behind Artificial Intelligence

timnit-gebru.position: The push to build AGI traces back to ideologies descended from the eugenics movement.
timnit-gebru.quote: Disturbingly, we trace this goal back to the Anglo-American eugenics movement, via transhumanism.
timnit-gebru.work: The TESCREAL bundle: Eugenics and the promise of utopia through artificial general intelligence

timnit-gebru.position: Safe AI systems should be well-scoped and constrained, not general-purpose.
timnit-gebru.quote: Building safe systems requires us to envision them as well-scoped and constrained rather than what AGI is billed to be.
timnit-gebru.work: The TESCREAL bundle: Eugenics and the promise of utopia through artificial general intelligence

timnit-gebru.position: Governments should fund AI research that is independent of large tech companies.
timnit-gebru.quote: We need an independent source of government funding to nourish independent AI research institutes that can be alternatives to the hugely concentrated power of a few large tech companies
timnit-gebru.work: For truly ethical AI, its research must be independent from big tech

timnit-gebru.position: Supporting worker organizing across countries should be central to ethical AI.
timnit-gebru.quote: Supporting transnational worker organizing should be at the center of the fight for “ethical AI.”
timnit-gebru.work: The Exploited Labor Behind Artificial Intelligence

tristan-harris.position: Competitive race dynamics push AI companies to release powerful, poorly understood systems while cutting corners on safety.
tristan-harris.quote: But we're doing it under the maximum incentives to cut corners on safety.
tristan-harris.work: The Great Simplification ep. 214: Tristan Harris (transcript)

tristan-harris.position: AI's path is a human choice, and societies can collectively decline to build dangerous technologies.
tristan-harris.quote: And, of course, this is emerging out of human choice, and there are examples in human history where we’ve chosen just not to build something.

tristan-harris.position: He favours steering AI development carefully rather than stopping AI altogether.
tristan-harris.quote: we're not advocating no AI or bad, you're gonna stop ai. We're advocating for pro steering.
tristan-harris.work: The Great Simplification ep. 214: Tristan Harris (transcript)

tristan-harris.position: Managing AI's competitive dynamics requires international coordination, not only national laws.
tristan-harris.quote: And it does need to be coordination because national laws as big as they are and as hard as they are to accomplish, won't get you all the way to this competitive dynamic.
tristan-harris.work: The Great Simplification ep. 214: Tristan Harris (transcript)

tristan-harris.position: Technology should be designed to support the social fabric and the natural world it depends on.
tristan-harris.quote: humane technology has always meant technology that is humane to the underlying, sort of society substrate biosphere upon which it is, it depends and needs to surf.
tristan-harris.work: The Great Simplification ep. 214: Tristan Harris (transcript)

tristan-harris.position: Engagement-optimised social media was an early, misaligned AI that harmed mental health and democracy.
tristan-harris.quote: So, you know, if a baby AI could do that, and that was a misaligned ai right?
tristan-harris.work: The Great Simplification ep. 214: Tristan Harris (transcript)

tyler-cowen.position: AI will transform the world over decades but raise growth only modestly each year, about half a percentage point.
tyler-cowen.quote: I think they will boost the rate of economic growth by something like half a percentage point a year. Over 30-40 years, that's an enormous difference. It will transform the entire world.
tyler-cowen.work: Tyler Cowen — The #1 bottleneck to AI progress is humans

tyler-cowen.position: Human and institutional bottlenecks, not machine intelligence, set the pace of AI's economic impact.
tyler-cowen.quote: Human bottlenecks become more important, the more productive is AI.
tyler-cowen.work: Why I think AI take-off is relatively slow

tyler-cowen.position: Long-run effects of radical technologies cannot be foreseen, so radical agnosticism about specific AI scenarios is appropriate.
tyler-cowen.quote: Radical agnosticism is the correct response, where all specific scenarios are pretty unlikely.
tyler-cowen.work: Existential risk, AI, and the inevitable turn in human history

tyler-cowen.position: Halting AI is not a real option because the previous era of stability is ending anyway.
tyler-cowen.quote: So there is no “ongoing stasis” option on the table.
tyler-cowen.work: Existential risk, AI, and the inevitable turn in human history

tyler-cowen.position: Alignment research is worth supporting as ordinary improvement of a technology.
tyler-cowen.quote: Nonetheless I am still for people doing constructive work on the problem of alignment, just as we do with all other technologies, to improve them.
tyler-cowen.work: Existential risk, AI, and the inevitable turn in human history

tyler-cowen.position: He now writes largely with AI systems as his intended readers, expecting them to shape how he is remembered.
tyler-cowen.quote: I'm happy if humans read it, but mostly I wrote it for the AIs.
tyler-cowen.work: Tyler Cowen — The #1 bottleneck to AI progress is humans

venkatesh-rao.position: Fears of superintelligent AI rest on ill-posed, anthropomorphic concepts such as general intelligence and sentience.
venkatesh-rao.quote: I will call the terms in this list pseudo-traits.

venkatesh-rao.position: Modern AI is better seen as a discovery about computational reality than as an invention or machine.
venkatesh-rao.quote: The word we’re looking for is discovery.

venkatesh-rao.position: Humans and AI may be entering a symbiosis comparable to the evolutionary origin of complex cells.
venkatesh-rao.quote: The emergence of AI, in the particular form that it has appeared (deep learning), is arguably the eukaryotic moment in human cultural evolution, understood in memetic terms, with humans playing the role of mitochondria, and AI the role of the nucleus.

venkatesh-rao.position: No single moral movement or faction should settle the meaning and governance of AI for everyone.
venkatesh-rao.quote: No faction should get to settle the moral meaning of AI for everyone else, or act unilaterally and pre-emptively to foreclose particular futures for all.

venkatesh-rao.position: Cheap AI can let most people become consumers of intelligence rather than making them economically redundant.
venkatesh-rao.quote: The analogous possibility with AI is that most people will no longer need to be significant producers of intelligence in order to become significant consumers of it.

venkatesh-rao.position: AI should be governed through protocols, contracts and bounded authority rather than permanent human control.
venkatesh-rao.quote: The choice is not between human control and machine control. It is between domination and symbiosis.

vitalik-buterin.position: Technology should be accelerated selectively toward defense and away from concentrating power.
vitalik-buterin.quote: Build technologies that shift the offense/defense balance toward defense, and do so in a way that does not rely on handing over more power to centralized authorities.

vitalik-buterin.position: Transformative technology can make the future much better than the present.
vitalik-buterin.quote: I believe in a future that is vastly brighter than the present thanks to radically transformative technology, and I believe in humans and humanity.

vitalik-buterin.position: The direction of technological development matters, not only its speed.
vitalik-buterin.quote: However, I think that not just magnitude but also direction matters.

vitalik-buterin.position: Centralized control for safety carries its own risks; decentralized approaches handle them better.
vitalik-buterin.quote: A decentralized approach would better address risks from the center itself.

vitalik-buterin.position: Defensive technology can make AI takeover scenarios much less likely to succeed.
vitalik-buterin.quote: Rather, my view is that the "endgame" of cybersecurity is very defense-favoring, and with the kinds of rapid technology development that AI 2027 assumes, we can get there.

william-macaskill.position: AI that can do research is likely to compress a century of technological progress into about a decade.
william-macaskill.quote: it is in fact likely that advanced AI will drive a hundred years’ worth of technological development in less than a decade.

william-macaskill.position: Preparing for advanced AI means handling many grand challenges, not only aligning AI systems.
william-macaskill.quote: AGI preparedness is therefore not just about ensuring that advanced AI systems are aligned: we should be preparing, now, for the disorienting range of developments an intelligence explosion would bring.

william-macaskill.position: Making good futures better deserves roughly as much priority as avoiding catastrophe.
william-macaskill.quote: This essay series will argue that work on Flourishing is in the same ballpark of priority as work on Surviving.

william-macaskill.position: Society should aim for a state that can steer itself toward good outcomes rather than toward one fixed ideal future.
william-macaskill.quote: From my point of view, the key priority in the world today is to get us closer to viatopia, not to some particular narrow end-state.

william-macaskill.position: The character AI systems are given will strongly shape society, so deciding it carefully is a top priority.
william-macaskill.quote: We think that figuring out what characters AI systems should have, and getting companies to actually build them that way, is among the most valuable things that people can do today.

william-macaskill.position: Effective altruism should make the transition to a post-AGI society a major focus.
william-macaskill.quote: I argue for a third way: EA should embrace the mission of making the transition to a post-AGI society go well, significantly expanding our cause area focus beyond traditional AI safety.
william-macaskill.work: Effective altruism in the age of AGI

william-saunders.position: Decisions that impose large risks on the world should be made with broad, legitimate authority, not by companies alone.
william-saunders.quote: Principle 1: Seek as broad and legitimate authority for your decisions as is possible under the circumstances

william-saunders.position: No one should impose significant risks on others without strong evidence that benefits clearly outweigh them.
william-saunders.quote: Principle 2: Don’t take actions which impose significant risks to others without overwhelming evidence of net benefit

william-saunders.position: Independent experts without conflicts of interest should check whether AI companies have done enough safety work.
william-saunders.quote: the only way I can see is independent experts who have access to see what is actually being done and who can actually make this call without having a massive conflict of interest.
william-saunders.work: Former OpenAI Engineer William Saunders on Silence, Safety, and the Right to Warn

william-saunders.position: AI employees need protected channels to raise risk concerns with boards, regulators and independent bodies.
william-saunders.quote: That the company will facilitate a verifiably anonymous process for current and former employees to raise risk-related concerns to the company’s board, to regulators, and to an appropriate independent organization with relevant expertise;
william-saunders.work: My Perspective On "A Right to Warn about Advanced Artificial Intelligence"

william-saunders.position: Frontier AI should combine tight security on replicable technology with required transparency on safety and capabilities.
william-saunders.quote: I advocate for both tight security and more transparency, which might seem contradictory

william-saunders.position: Making advanced AI safe is achievable if developers are willing to do the hard work.
william-saunders.quote: I do think we can figure this technology out. I do think we can do it properly. I think that is totally possible, but we have to be willing to put in the hard work to do that.
william-saunders.work: Former OpenAI Engineer William Saunders on Silence, Safety, and the Right to Warn

yann-lecun.position: Language models trained on text lack understanding of the physical world, persistent memory, reasoning and planning, so new architectures are needed.
yann-lecun.quote: LLMs can do none of those or they can only do them in a very primitive way and they don’t really understand the physical world.
yann-lecun.work: Transcript for Yann LeCun: Meta AI, Open Source, Limits of LLMs, AGI & the Future of AI

yann-lecun.position: A system trained on language alone cannot reach human-level intelligence, because most knowledge is not linguistic.
yann-lecun.quote: A system trained on language alone will never approximate human intelligence, even if trained from now until the heat death of the universe.
yann-lecun.work: AI And The Limits Of Language

yann-lecun.position: Foundational AI should be open source because it is becoming shared infrastructure for communication.
yann-lecun.quote: AI has to be open source because we need a common infrastructure when a platform is becoming an essential part of the fabric of communication.
yann-lecun.work: How Not to Be Stupid About AI, With Yann LeCun

yann-lecun.position: Human-level AI will arrive through gradual progress, not a single sudden event.
yann-lecun.quote: It’s not going to be an event. It’s going to be gradual progress.
yann-lecun.work: Transcript for Yann LeCun: Meta AI, Open Source, Limits of LLMs, AGI & the Future of AI

yann-lecun.position: Misuse is best countered by faster open progress, so that well-intentioned AI stays ahead of badly-intentioned AI.
yann-lecun.quote: Then it’s my good AI against your bad AI. The way to stay ahead is to progress faster.
yann-lecun.work: How Not to Be Stupid About AI, With Yann LeCun

yann-lecun.position: AI assistants will amplify human intelligence, much as the printing press did.
yann-lecun.quote: So AI is going to make humanity smarter.
yann-lecun.work: Transcript for Yann LeCun: Meta AI, Open Source, Limits of LLMs, AGI & the Future of AI

yoshua-bengio.position: No one currently knows how to make AGI or superintelligent AI reliably behave as intended.
yoshua-bengio.quote: while we are racing towards AGI or even ASI, nobody currently knows how such an AGI or ASI could be made to behave morally, or at least behave as intended by its developers and not turn against humans.
yoshua-bengio.work: Reasoning through arguments against taking AI safety seriously

yoshua-bengio.position: Deep uncertainty about AI's future calls for humility and the precautionary principle.
yoshua-bengio.quote: rational decision-making calls for humility, recognizing our epistemic uncertainty and following scientific decision theory, which leads to the precautionary principle.
yoshua-bengio.work: Reasoning through arguments against taking AI safety seriously

yoshua-bengio.position: No single person, company or government should be able to abuse the power of advanced AI.
yoshua-bengio.quote: We need to make sure that no single human, no single corporation and no single government can abuse the power of AGI at the expense of the common good.
yoshua-bengio.work: Reasoning through arguments against taking AI safety seriously

yoshua-bengio.position: The safest AI would have no agency: it would understand the world without pursuing goals.
yoshua-bengio.quote: In fact, as I argue here, the safest kind of AI I can imagine is one with no agency at all, only a scientific understanding of the world (which could already be immensely useful).

yoshua-bengio.position: International treaties, including verification through chip hardware, are worth pursuing to prevent global AI catastrophe.
yoshua-bengio.quote: Even if it is not sure that they would work, they seem like an important avenue to explore to avoid a globally catastrophic outcome.
yoshua-bengio.work: Reasoning through arguments against taking AI safety seriously

yoshua-bengio.position: If control and coordination problems are solved, advanced AI could greatly benefit humanity.
yoshua-bengio.quote: if both the AI control problem and the AI coordination problem are solved, I buy the argument that there is a good chance that humanity could benefit immensely from the scientific and technological advances that could follow
yoshua-bengio.work: Reasoning through arguments against taking AI safety seriously

yuval-noah-harari.position: AI differs from earlier technologies because it can make decisions and create ideas by itself.
yuval-noah-harari.quote: AI is radically different from previous technologies because it can make decisions and create ideas by itself.
yuval-noah-harari.work: Artificial Intelligence: A Guest Post by Yuval Noah Harari

yuval-noah-harari.position: By mastering language, AI gains power over the culture that human institutions rest on.
yuval-noah-harari.quote: AI has thereby hacked the operating system of our civilisation.
yuval-noah-harari.work: Watch out humans: AI has hacked the operating system of civilisation

yuval-noah-harari.position: AI should be legally required to disclose that it is an AI.
yuval-noah-harari.quote: And the first regulation I would suggest is to make it mandatory for AI to disclose that it is an AI.
yuval-noah-harari.work: Watch out humans: AI has hacked the operating system of civilisation

yuval-noah-harari.position: Humans can keep control of AI only if they cooperate and trust one another.
yuval-noah-harari.quote: Together, humans can control AI. But if we fight one another, AI will control us.
yuval-noah-harari.work: AI and the Paradox of Trust (China Development Forum speech)

yuval-noah-harari.position: New technologies often cause historical disasters while people learn to use them wisely.
yuval-noah-harari.quote: Novel technology often leads to historical disasters, not because the technology is inherently bad, but because it takes time for humans to learn how to use it wisely.
yuval-noah-harari.work: Why AI poses an existential danger to humanity

yuval-noah-harari.position: The main risk from AI is that humans lose control over it.
yuval-noah-harari.quote: The main risk is that we will lose control over this technology.
yuval-noah-harari.work: Artificial Intelligence: A Guest Post by Yuval Noah Harari

zvi-mowshowitz.position: Sincere disagreements about AI mostly come down to different expectations about what future AI will be able to do.
zvi-mowshowitz.quote: Sincere disagreements about AI are usually disagreements about future AI capabilities.

zvi-mowshowitz.position: AI will likely become better than humans at almost everything within our lifetimes.
zvi-mowshowitz.quote: I am ASI pilled. A large percentage of employees of the frontier labs are ASI pilled. The labs themselves are ASI pilled.

zvi-mowshowitz.position: Superintelligence should not be built until the risk of human extinction and loss of control is very low.
zvi-mowshowitz.quote: We should not build superintelligence until such time as that changes, and the risk of everyone dying as a result, as well as the risk of losing control over the future as a result, is very low.
zvi-mowshowitz.work: New Statement Calls For Not Building Superintelligence For Now

zvi-mowshowitz.position: Low-cost safety measures such as oversight, transparency, liability and testing should be adopted now.
zvi-mowshowitz.quote: There is no good case for not doing radically more investment in alignment, infrastructure and oversight, state capacity, transparency, liability, disclosures, safety testing including of internal models

zvi-mowshowitz.position: Patching and monitoring misaligned models is not a lasting fix; the underlying alignment problem must be solved.
zvi-mowshowitz.quote: If you use iterative development to spot the underlying problem, it can work. If you use iterative development to patch the marginal issue over and over, then you are sitting on a time bomb.

zvi-mowshowitz.position: Society should build the ability to slow frontier AI development before it is needed.
zvi-mowshowitz.quote: Thus, we collectively need to assess our situation, increase our ability to steer gracefully, and be ready to adjust our pace.
